Ensign Reyes. Thin, filthy, and asking for coffee.
Ensign Novak. Walked onto the pad on her own feet.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_ensigns_wel: I'm going to bring her something from the galley.
Bring her socks. Surface socks are terrible.
I'll tell her the whole deck says welcome home.
I'll bring socks. And the gossip. She's missed five months of it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_ensigns_who: Is she all right? Is she hurt?
The Doctor says tired, dehydrated, nothing that won't mend.
Sickbay. She's sleeping. She keeps waking up to check she's aboard.
Oh, that's good. That's so good.
She asked if we'd kept her quarters. We had. Nobody touched anything.
First thing she asked for was a shower. Then the date. Then the others.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_watcher_lea: All right. You don't have to.
Want company? Or want me to go?
I can go, if you'd rather.
Go. It's all right. I just need a minute.
I'm all right. Honestly. Thank you for asking.
I'm on deck three if you change your mind.
Find me later. I mean it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_watcher_pus: You were on sensors in June, weren't you?
Two days. I watched it all. The whole county. Two days.
I had the long-range sensors. I counted lights going out.
That's not a thing anybody should have to watch.
We couldn't do anything. Observe only. I observed.
Observe only. That was the order. So I observed. All of it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_watcher_sit: They were people. They had radios and markets and school buses.
There was a baseball game on the Friday. I heard the crowd on the audio.
They were real. All of them.
Nobody ever says that. People say the county. I want to say the people.
I don't want them to just be a number I watched.
Then say it. I'll listen. Any time.
They were people. I'll remember too.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_watcher_sta: You all right? You've been staring at that bulkhead a while.
You don't look fine. Sit a second.
Do you want to talk about it?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_watcher_tre: Have you talked to Counselor Tren?
Tren's got a free slot on Thursdays.
Once. She was very kind. She said it's allowed to hurt.
Not yet. I'll go. I keep meaning to go.
Go. For me, if not for you.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_the_watcher_wal: Come on. I'll walk you to the galley. Grieg's got soup.
Walk with me. You shouldn't be on your own right now.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_transporter_ner: What helps? What do you do?
Is there anything that helps?
I count. Backwards from twenty. My grandmother taught me.
I close my eyes and I think about the coffee at the other end.
Then count. And there'll be coffee. I'll make sure.
Tell the pad chief. Everyone's got something. They'll wait for you.
No. I'll go. Somebody's got to. The eleven went down every day.
I'll do it. If Shepard did it every day for five months, I can do it once.
That's the spirit. I'll wave from the console.
I'll be at the pad. Promise.
Wave with both hands. So I know I've come back in one piece.
If I come back as two people, you're buying both of them dinner.
Deal.
Done. Both of you.
Look at it this way. You get a free scrub. Atom by atom.
Think of it as the most thorough sonic shower you'll ever have.
That doesn't help. That's worse.
Why would you say that?
Sorry. That one's for engineers.
Yes. Sorry. Wrong audience.
It's the best-behaved system on the ship. It's never dropped anybody.
Th'Zoran runs those pads like a clock. You'll be fine.
It's not the dropping. It's the being taken apart and put back.
Yes, but is it me that comes back? That's what I think about.
It's you. I've seen you before and after. Same terrible haircut.
It's you. The same you. I promise. I've read the physics.
They've put me on the survey detail. Beaming down. Tomorrow.
I've been assigned to the pad team. They want me to beam.
Congratulations? You look like I said congratulations to a funeral.
That's good news. Isn't it? You've gone green.
I hate transporters. I really, deeply hate transporters.
I have never liked being taken apart. It's a thing. It's a personal thing.
Could I swap? With somebody else?
Is it cowardly to ask to swap?
Not cowardly. Ask. But I think you'd do fine.
Ask the Lieutenant. She'll say yes. But you might regret it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_which_deck_chat: Did you see the surface on the viewer this morning?
They put the planet on the lounge viewer again. Clear day.
Clouds over the county. Looked almost normal from up here.
I saw. Green. It looks so green, still.
It does. From here you'd never know.
I keep looking for the towns at night. The lights.
I don't look any more. I used to look every morning.
I still look. Out of habit.
Me too. I can't help it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_which_deck_join: Thanks. I'm late for the transporter schedule. Th'Zoran will kill me.
Thank you. Sickbay. I've got samples. Don't bump me.
Kess only kills people on Tuesdays.
That's very kind. Very still, everyone.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_which_deck_quie: What are you on, this week?
Could be worse. Could be tube seven.
Somebody has to count the spoons.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_cor_which_deck_stuc: Deck three junction. It does this. Give it a second.
It's the junction. Engineering rerouted the lift power.
Is there a hatch? There's always a hatch.
Give it ten seconds. It sulks.
There's a hatch. We are not using the hatch.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_1: I'll tell Grieg. She'll forgive you by dinner.
Thank you. I'll tell the galley. They'll send you something.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_2: Log it. Nineteen, fused, bypassed. Diagnostic one hundred.
Logging it. I'll put a star next to the hundredth.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_3: When we get home I'm framing that conduit.
Next week: a hundred and one.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_4: While I've got you both: the bypass. Does it hold if the pads fire?
One question. Does the reroute take a transporter surge?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_5: Good question. Let me look. ... Yes. With room.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_6: Then I'm happy. If the pads go down, everybody on this ship notices.
Good. The pads are the one thing that can't go dark.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_close_7: The pads get power before anything. Before us. Before the galley.
Transporter first. Always. That's the chief's first rule.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_diag_1_: Level three diagnostic, conduit nineteen, run... let me see.
Starting the diagnostic. Look at the counter.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_diag_3_: This is the hundredth. The hundredth time I've run this exact test.
One hundred. We have hit a hundred. On the same conduit.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_diag_4_: Somebody should get you a certificate.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_diag_5_: And it'll say what it said the other ninety-nine times.
It will say nothing is wrong. As it always says.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_1_2: Nineteen? I heard you from the lift.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_1_3: Is that the conduit? The galley lost power to the oven.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_2_1: It did. The diagnostic says it didn't.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_2_2: It did, {c}. The test says otherwise.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_3_1: Then stop testing it and replace it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_3_2: Can we just swap the whole run?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_4_1: With what? We don't have another run. We have what came on board.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_4_2: We haven't got a spare run. We haven't got a starbase.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_5_1: The shuttle bay stores might. Or somebody's been hoarding.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_ops_5_2: Ask the chief. Rhel knows where every bolt on this ship is.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_result_: Result: nominal. Of course it's nominal.
It fused an hour ago. How is it nominal?
It's lying. The conduit is lying to us.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_rhel_1_: The chief says he'll bless it. He'll put his hand on it and swear at it.
Rhel said to talk to it nicely. I think he meant it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_rhel_3_: More often than the diagnostic does.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_rip_1_1: Right. We bypass it. Route through eighteen and twenty.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_rip_1_2: We reroute. Eighteen can carry the load if twenty helps.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_rip_3_1: Warm we can live with. Out we can't.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_rip_4_1: Doing it. ... Rerouted. Galley has power.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_start_1: Nineteen's gone again. Third time this week.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_why_1_1: Why does it keep fusing? The load's nowhere near its rating.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_why_1_2: It shouldn't fuse. It's carrying a third of what it's rated for.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_why_2_1: Because it was in the path on the ninth. It took a surge nobody logged.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_conduit_why_2_2: Because the whole run got cooked in February. It's tired.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_dilithium_ledge: Is that the ledger?
Morning. Tell me something I want to hear.
Don't get up. What's the count?
One in, two spares, one up from the surface this week, Captain's aide.
We're holding, {c}. Thanks to someone below.
Holding is good. Holding is the whole job right now.
Good. The Captain will want the surface one flagged.
Flagged. With where it was found.
Already flagged. Open ground, again.
Of course it was.
Naturally. The planet has manners.
Everything's a countdown. The trick is making it a long one.
It's always been a clock. We just used to have a starbase at the end.
How long, at this rate?
Give me a date.
I'm not giving you a date. Last time I did, it went round the deck.
No dates. Rhel banned dates after someone put one on the mess wall.
Fair.
Wise.
I'll post the numbers. No dates.
Ledger's filed. Biscuit's yours.
Thank you. And thank whoever's down there.
Good work. Both of you.
One a week. If that holds, we're not on a clock at all.
If the surface keeps sending, we stop counting down.
If.
That's a big if, {c}.
I know. Let me have it until lunch.
Everything's a big if. Let me have this one.
Until lunch. Then back to the countdown.
Deal.
Walk me to the rack. I want to see them.
Show me the spares. I like to look at them.
They're crystals, {a}. They look like crystals.
They're in a locked box. They look like a locked box.
Humour me. Some people count their money.
I sleep better after.
The replicator ration stays where it is, then.
We keep the replicator ration. Nobody's going to like hearing it.
Nobody likes it now. They'll dislike it at the same level.
Grieg will be pleased. More people eating her cooking.
I'll tell the Captain. She'll want to see your face when she hears.
I'll pass it up. Keep trimming.
Crystal count for the week. You want the good news or the numbers?
I did the dilithium ledger. Sit down first.
Morning. I brought the crystal count. And a biscuit, to soften it.
Numbers. The good news is always a lie.
Just the numbers, {b}.
One in the core. Spares on the rack. And the burn rate hasn't moved.
The core's at about half on the current crystal. Two spares on the rack.
So it's a countdown.
So we are, as always, on a clock.
What came up from the surface this week?
Anything beamed up from below?
One crystal. Transporter room logged it on Tuesday.
One. Somebody down there walked it to a pad and we pulled it up.
Somebody.
Who?
Nobody knows. Th'Zoran says the signal's odd. Never the same place twice.
Kess says don't ask. Whoever it is, bless them.
I'd like to thank them. Whoever's doing it.
Someone down there's keeping us lit.
The transporter crew wave at the pad every time. Just in case.
Kess leaves the channel open a few seconds longer. In case they say hello.
That's nice. That's very Starfleet.
Good. Somebody should say it.
Where did they find it?
Was it the same pattern?
Same as always. Open ground. A field off a county road.
Woods, north of one of the towns. Never in the town. Never once.
Never under a town. Not a single one. Has science got anywhere with that?
That's still the strangest thing on this whole survey.
Science says it's statistically absurd, and then they go quiet.
Science has three theories and hates all of them.
Crystals don't care where people put their houses.
Dilithium doesn't know what a town is. It shouldn't.
These seem to.
Apparently here it does.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_clea: Flange is clean. Seal's in. Clamps back on.
Marks lined up. And I counted every tool. Twice.
All tools out. I counted them back into the case.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_conf: Honestly? I've done it in the simulator forty times.
I've read the manual. Twice. I've got this.
The manual's never been on this ship.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_fini: A waste reclamation valve on the Ticonderoga. I cried a bit. Don't tell.
A sonic shower on a starbase. Nobody died. The admiral got very clean.
I won't tell.
Your secret's safe.
Go on. Write it up. Put your name on it. Your name, not mine.
Log it yourself. First solo. You'll want to read it back one day.
Yes, {a}. Thank you. Really.
Thank you. For not taking the spanner off me.
Bringing the loop back up.
Restoring the loop.
Pressure?
Numbers?
Holding. It's holding.
Nominal. It's nominal. Oh, it's nominal.
Congratulations, {b}. You just kept a hundred and forty-one people breathing.
That's it. First solo. You kept the air on.
Don't say it like that!
Can I sit down now?
Sit down. I'll tell the chief. He'll pretend he isn't pleased.
I'll tell Rhel. He'll nod. That's the highest honour he gives.
My hands are shaking. Is that normal?
Why are my hands shaking now?
Completely normal. Mine shook for a week after my first.
That's the adrenaline. It comes after. It always comes after.
What was your first?
Do you remember yours?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_mist: The flange is pitted. Badly. The seal won't take.
It's pitted. The manual says replace the flange. We don't have a flange.
Good. You checked. Most people don't. Now: what do you do?
You found it. That's the job. What are your options?
I could... dress it? File the pitting smooth, and double the seal.
Lap it down. Two seals, offset. The way the chief did the aft loop.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_nerv: What if I get it wrong? It's the coupling for the environmental loop.
It's the air, {a}. If I get it wrong, it's the air.
If you get it wrong, the backup takes over and I come and help.
There's a backup. There's always a backup. That's what engineering is.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_pep_: Breathe. You know what the chief said to me on my first?
Hey. Look at me. You passed the Academy. This is just a seal.
He said: the ship doesn't know you're new. So don't tell her.
He said: if you're scared, you're paying attention. Good.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_first_solo_star: Is that... your first solo repair?
Is it true you're doing the coupling alone?
Chief put you on the coupling by yourself? Congratulations.
Yes. Please don't watch.
It is. I'm fine. I'm totally fine.
He did. I think he forgot I'm new.
He doesn't forget anything. He thinks you're ready.
Rhel doesn't forget. He picked you.
Isolating the loop. ... Isolated.
Taking it offline. Offline.
Good. Now tell me what you're going to do before you do it.
Talk me through it. Out loud. It helps.
Release the clamps, withdraw the old seal, check the flange for pitting.
Clamps, seal, flange. Then the new seal. Then clamps again.
And?
And what do you check before you close it?
That I haven't left a tool in it.
Alignment marks.
That the new seal isn't upside down.
Good. Go.
Correct. Go on.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_jefferies_crawl: Why is it always the tubes? Why is nothing ever broken in a nice wide room?
Nothing ever breaks in a corridor. It's always forty metres into a tube.
Because the designers were cruel.
Because the ship hates us.
I'm writing to the Corps of Engineers. When comms are back.
Put it in the letters we can't send.
I'm in. It's warm. Why is it warm?
Going up. Keep talking to me.
Probably the conduit.
You're fine. You've got two metres before the bend.
Tell me something. Anything. The tubes are too quiet.
Talk to me. I hate how quiet it gets in here.
Grieg's doing a real stew tonight. With actual potatoes from the surface.
Pell Daro bet me the helm would move again before the new year.
Good. Keep going.
That's nice. More of that.
That's all I've got. Rations and gossip.
I'm out. Sing something?
Absolutely not.
Never. ... Hang on.
Found the junction. There's a burn mark. Wasn't here last month.
Junction box. It's scorched. Somebody's going to hear about this.
Scorched how?
Old burn or new?
Old relay's out. New one's in. Seating it.
Clipping it in. Tell me when the board goes green.
Board's... amber. ... Green. It's green.
Amber. Hold on. ... Green. You're green.
Good. I'm coming down before this tube eats me.
Coming down. Grab my foot if I slide.
Hatch is sticking.
Help me with this. It's jammed again.
On three. One. Two.
Put your shoulder into it.
There. Pass me the light. And the tricorder. And the spanner.
Light. Tricorder. The small spanner, not that one.
How many engineers does it take to change a relay?
Knock knock.
I said no jokes.
I will come down there.
Fine. Silence. Engineering silence.
Sorry. Go on.
New. Last week, maybe. A relay's been arcing.
Fresh. A relay arcing every time somebody runs the replicators.
That's the replicator line?
That'll be the galley draw.
Every time Grieg's lot run the big replicator, this goes pop.
So every lunchtime this little box has a small fire.
Can you fix it from in there?
Can you swap it?
I've got a spare. Give me five minutes and no jokes.
Pass up the spare relay. And don't be funny.
Old. It's been here since February.
Old. Months old. Look at the carbon.
February?
From the ninth?
Could be. Everything on the ninth arced somewhere.
Everything tripped at once that night. This is where it landed.
Then why's it faulting now?
And it's only started faulting now?
Because it's been cooking for five months and nobody crawled up here.
Because we fix what shouts. This one's been whispering.
You've got soot on your face.
Your whole face is black.
Leave it. It's how they know I did something.
That's my medal. Leave it.
I'll log it. Tube seven, relay, you, very brave.
Logged. You want the shower first, or the galley?
Shower. Then the galley. Then sleep. In that order.
Galley. I'll eat with the soot. It adds flavour.
Shower's on the ration too, remember. Sonic only till Thursday.
Water ration. Sonic shower. Sorry.
Then I'll sonic the soot and keep the dignity.
I'll take the sonic.
I'll tell Grieg to save you a bowl. She likes a tube crawler.
Grieg saves a bowl for anyone who's been up a tube. It's a rule.
Tell her it was tube seven. She'll give me extra.
Tell her I suffered. Tell her I suffered a lot.
Consider it done. Go on.
Go. Before the chief finds you another tube.
Tube seven. Junction box on the second level is throwing faults.
Somebody's got to crawl tube seven. Guess who.
Right. Who wants to go in the tube?
I did the last one.
Not it.
I crawled tube four yesterday. My knees filed a complaint.
Then you can hold my feet.
Fine. You're on the hatch.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_like_a_surgeon_: Have you shown the chief?
Does Rhel know you're doing this?
He built half of it with me. At three in the morning.
He watched it once. Then he went and sat with the core for an hour.
What did he say?
Did he say anything?
Whoever it was, they've been in an engine room before. That's all.
Only that they knew her. Knew her like one of us would.
I'll keep it in the simulator. For now.
I'll keep working on it. Quietly.
Quietly is good.
Get some sleep first.
And lock that simulation. Nobody else needs a nightmare.
Send me a copy. Not the Captain. Me.
Why you and not the Captain?
You don't want the Captain to see it?
She's seen it. She saw it the day after. She knows what it looks like.
Because she already knows. She's had her own copy since February.
Then why hasn't she said anything?
And she's never said?
Because saying it doesn't get us anything but scared of each other.
Because a ship this size can't afford to look over its shoulder.
Understood. I'll send it to you. Only you.
All right. Just you.
And then we go and get something to eat. Something real.
And then you sleep. Actual sleep. Not simulator sleep.
Warp: the intermix controller, and nothing else. Impulse: the regulators.
Two cuts. Only two. Warp controller, impulse regulators.
And the rest of the ship?
And everything else?
Untouched. Life support, the core, the transporter, the replicators.
Not a scratch. Air, power, food, the pads. All of it left for us.
Some of the science deck say Q. A whole planet from nowhere, why not us?
The Q theory's gaining ground in the science labs.
Sensible people believe it. I'm not sure it explains a fused regulator.
A Q wouldn't need regulators. It'd just snap its fingers.
That's what I keep saying. This was hands. Tools. Knowledge.
Whoever did this held a spanner. I'd bet my rank on it.
Section 31 would know how to blind a ship.
That'd fit, wouldn't it?
It'd fit. A lot of things fit. That's the trouble with this one.
Maybe. But Okafor looked genuinely rattled when she said it.
Rattled how?
You saw that?
Like a man who'd just found out he wasn't the worst thing in the room.
Like somebody who'd been blindsided too. I don't know. Drop it.
I heard sickbay found something odd in the samples. From the surface.
Someone in the medical lab said the markers were confusing.
I've heard that too. And I've heard the Doctor say he can support the
Me too. Anwar's been quiet. The Doctor said something about chemistry,
chemistry but not the author. Whatever that means.
and not the author. Nobody knows what he meant.
That's a strange thing for a hologram to say.
That's unsettling.
I pulled the damage map from the ninth up again.
I've been rebuilding the ninth in the simulator. Step by step.
Why do that to yourself?
Of course you have.
Because it bothers me. Not that it happened. How it happened.
Because it wasn't vandalism. Look at it. Just look.
It's like somebody who knew exactly how to blind a ship.
Like a surgeon. Cut the nerve, leave the patient breathing.
Yes. That's it. Blind it, don't kill it.
Exactly. Stranded, not dead.
Why would anyone want that?
Who wants a witness that can't leave?
I don't know. That's the bit that keeps me up.
I've got no idea.
I'd be careful putting that in a report.
Is this for the Captain?
You're doing security's job again.
It's just a simulation, {c}. I'm not accusing anyone.
Nobody's being named. I just want to understand it.
Everybody has a theory. Mine changes every week.
You know Shepard thought Section 31. That was her whole theory.
Maybe they didn't have time for more.
Maybe they got interrupted.
Ninety seconds, and it was over. They weren't rushed. They were finished.
They had time. They used exactly what they needed. Nothing more.
That's a very tidy saboteur.
That's cold.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_nursing_the_cor: Log it. Point oh three, trimmed, holding. My name on it.
Put it in the log. And set an alarm for the next check.
Logged. Want coffee?
Logged. I'll bring you a coffee. Real one, if Grieg will.
Please. And stand there a minute longer. I like the company.
Yes. Then come back and watch her with me.
Do you ever think about what she'd be like at warp again?
What was she like? At full warp. Before.
Loud. Bright. She sang. You could feel it in your back teeth.
Beautiful. The whole deck hummed. You could hear it in the lifts.
I only came aboard in December. I barely heard her.
I miss it and I barely remember it.
You'll hear it again. The chief says so, and he doesn't say things.
You will. One day. I'm keeping her ready for it.
Coffee. Right. Back in five.
Five minutes. Don't let her drift.
She won't. Not on my watch.
I've got her. Go.
While you're in there: sickbay wants more power for the lab.
Sickbay's asking for another two percent. For the samples.
Of course they are.
Everyone wants two percent.
Tell Dr. Anwar she can have one, and I'll owe her the other.
Tell them yes. The samples matter. The survivors' samples.
The Doctor will complain that one percent is an insult.
He'll sulk.
The Doctor is a hologram. He can sulk at one percent.
He can sulk in a lower power state.
What's that do to the reserve?
How's the reserve looking, after that?
Better than it was. We just stopped wasting a sliver of crystal.
A little better. Every trim buys us a few hours further out.
Hours.
A few hours. You say that like it's a lot.
Out here, it is. Hours add up to days. Days add up to a crystal.
It is a lot. Everything's a lot now. We don't make more crystal.
Rhel said he'd be down to look at her himself.
Is the chief coming? He'll want to see this.
He was here at oh-four-hundred. He's always here at oh-four-hundred.
The chief's asleep. First time in three days. Nobody wake him.
You're going to do it without him?
You sure you want to do this alone?
He taught me. And he'd want me to try before I woke him.
I've watched him do it forty times. I can do it once.
You're watching her like she's a patient.
You look like you're sitting with somebody in hospital.
She is a patient. She's the only one on this ship who keeps us all alive.
She is. She's the lights and the air and the transporter. She's everything.
When you put it like that.
Point taken. I'll be nicer to her.
Everybody should be nicer to her.
Tell the others.
Intermix is drifting again. Point oh three.
She's running warm. Look at the matter stream.
Come look at this. No, don't touch it. Just look.
Is that bad? Tell me that's not bad.
That's... within tolerance. Isn't it?
It's within tolerance. It's also not what she did yesterday.
It's fine. It's fine the way a cough is fine.
Should I call the chief?
Do you want me to page anyone?
Not yet. Let me look at her properly first.
No. Stand there and read me numbers. That's all I need.
I'm going to walk the antimatter flow down. Slowly.
Hand me the injector readout. I'm trimming the flow.
How slowly?
Should I tell the bridge?
Want me to hold the display?
Slowly like you're moving a sleeping cat.
One increment every ten seconds. Read me the chamber pressure.
Pressure's holding. ... Still holding.
Holding. Holding. Still holding.
There. She settles. See the ripple smooth out?
There she is. Good girl.
Why does she drift at all? We're not going anywhere.
What's she drifting for? It's not like we're at warp.
That's why. A core's built to push. We've had her idling five months.
She was built to run hard. Idle is what's killing her, bit by bit.
Like a horse in a stall.
Like a Klingon on shore leave.
Exactly like that. She wants to run and we won't let her.
Yes, and about as happy. Hand me the readout.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_replicator_budg: So: lab untouched, holodeck on rota, galley more stoves, lights down.
That's it, then. Lab stays, holodeck rota, stoves, dim the empty decks.
Agreed. The Captain will change one thing just to show she read it.
Agreed. Send it up.
She'll add a coffee exemption. She always does.
I hope she does. We all need it.
Anybody want to argue anything else while we're all in one room?
Last chance. Any other complaints?
The lift on deck three smells of burnt toast.
The sonic showers on deck two are set to scour.
That's not a power issue.
That's for maintenance, not us.
It's an issue. I'm raising it.
Everything's a power issue if you squint.
Noted. Ignored. Meeting over.
Logged under miscellaneous. Goodbye.
Thank you both. Genuinely. That was the nicest one of these we've had.
Thanks. Nobody cried this time. That's progress.
Then something else has to give.
We need to find the difference somewhere.
Lights in the unused quarters. The lower cargo bay.
The empty labs.
The shuttle bay. It's half heated for no reason.
We heat the whole shuttle bay for one old shuttle and a pile of chairs.
Don't start. You know that's a whole other fight.
Oh, you're brave.
Grieg wants less replicator and more real stoves.
Grieg says real cooking uses less power than people think.
She's right, actually. An oven is cheaper than a replicator per meal.
She's not wrong. A pot of stew beats a hundred replicated bowls.
People want what they want, though. Comfort food. Their own food.
Morale, {a}. People need a taste of home sometimes.
They can have it on their birthday.
One replicated treat a week.
And the holodeck. People are climbing the walls.
The holodeck hours. Tren says they matter. She put it in writing.
The holodeck eats power like nothing else.
A holodeck hour is a lot of crystal.
So is a crewman who hasn't seen a sky in five months.
So is a crewman who breaks down on shift.
... Fine. Two hours a week, per person, rota.
Point taken. We keep it.
The survivor samples need cold storage and the sequencers need power.
Every rescued ensign comes up with samples. We can't keep them on ice.
I know. You'll get it. Nobody argues with the lab.
That's fine. That's the one nobody's cutting.
Thank you. I expected more of a fight.
Oh. Good. I had a speech.
Save the speech. The galley's next.
Keep the speech. You'll need it.
It's Shepard's shuttle. It has a sofa in it. A sofa, {a}.
Lieutenant Shepard's shuttle has a refrigerator. An old one.
It's a field collection. It's the most important survey data we have.
That sofa is ethnography. I will die on this hill.
The sofa stays warm. Next.
We are not freezing the sofa. Next.
Replicator allocation. We have to agree it before the Captain does.
Right. Power budget. Who wants to go first?
The replicator schedule. Again. Somebody bring the list.
The core gives what it gives. The pie doesn't get bigger.
Same pie. Same slices. Everybody wants a bigger slice.
I've got eleven requests on this padd. Eleven.
Twelve requests this week.
Read them out.
Go on, then. The top of the list.
More replicator time, more holodeck, more hot water, and a cello.
Hot water, holodeck, the lab, and somebody wants a replicated cello.
A cello?
Somebody asked for what?
For the concert. There's going to be a concert. Apparently.
Lieutenant Tren says music's good for morale. She's not wrong.
Put the cello last. I like the cello, but put it last.
Fine. The cello goes on the list. At the bottom. With love.
Sciences needs its share for the lab. I'll say it now.
Sciences wants lab time.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_dec: Proposal to the first officer by end of shift, then.
I'll write it up. Hydroponics, a bench, a shuttle, and a sofa.
Here's what I'll take up. Half the bay for hydroponics. The shuttle stays.
Proposal: hydroponics along the port side. The shuttle keeps her corner.
And nobody touches her things.
And the furniture stays in the shuttle.
And I get one bench for fabrication.
Fine. But I want a workbench.
One bench. And ask her, first. Politely.
Agreed. Somebody ask her. Kindly.
I'll ask her. She'll talk to me. We're both from the lab side.
Let me ask. She's had a hard few months. She should hear it from a friend.
Tell her we'll keep her refrigerator running. That might win her over.
Tell her the adapter is safe. Tell her I admire the adapter.
I'll tell her you called it brilliant.
I'll tell her you used the word clever.
I did not say brilliant.
I said it was brilliant and I hated it.
She'll only hear the first half.
I'll leave out the second part.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_fur: There's a sofa. There's a television. There is a chair she won't let anyone
It has a sofa, a stove, and a theatre chair that nobody is allowed to
She's never said. Leave her the chair.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_hac: The adapter's made out of a toaster and a Starfleet coupling.
Half of it is a surface power strip. Half is a phase regulator.
She's a survey specialist. She makes do.
The chief wants to put it in the training manual. As a warning.
Rhel looked at it for a long time and then said, very quietly, clever.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_hyd: Real crops. Real food. Grieg's already drawn a plan.
Hydroponics. Soybeans, potatoes. Less replicator, less crystal.
That's the best argument I've heard all week.
The shuttle's been below half the time anyway.
It goes down, where it lives.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_pow: And have you seen what she did to the power bus?
She hung surface appliances off the shuttle's bus. Through an adapter.
She ran a 1990s refrigerator off a shuttle's EPS. With an adapter she made.
It works perfectly. That's what upsets me.
It's brilliant and I hate it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_she: That shuttle is her field station. She spent five months on that planet.
It's a working field station, {a}. With a refrigerator from 1993.
Has anybody actually asked Lieutenant Shepard?
She's been in with the Doctor since she came up. Nobody's had the nerve.
I tried. She talked for forty minutes about a lamp.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_sta: The first officer's asked for proposals on the shuttle bay.
Command wants the shuttle bay used for something. Ideas?
Right. The shuttle bay. We're finally having this conversation.
Hydroponics. It's the only open floor we've got that can take the weight.
A second workshop. We're tripping over each other in here.
It's got a shuttle in it. A historically significant shuttle.
Lieutenant Shepard's shuttle is in it. You can't just move her shuttle.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_shuttle_bay_wor: We need space to fabricate. The regulators, the conduit runs.
We need somewhere to build parts that aren't the core room.
From what we salvage. From what comes up the transporter.
You'd strip the shuttle for parts. Admit it.
I'd never. Well. Not all of it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_talking_to_her_: What do you say to it?
Does it help?
Mostly I tell her what's going on. The surface. The count.
Mostly I apologise. For February. For leaving her to idle.
You apologise to the core.
For February?
Somebody should. It wasn't her fault.
She didn't choose any of it.
Does she ever answer?
Has she ever said anything back?
Not in words. But you learn her. The sounds she makes before she drifts.
In her way. There's a tick in the housing before she runs warm.
A tick.
What kind of tick?
Listen. ... There. That's her being fine.
Hear that? That's contentment.
I don't hear anything.
That's the ventilation.
Give it five months. You'll hear it.
You will. Give it time.
Don't tell the Vulcans.
Don't tell security. They'll put it in my file.
Your secret's safe with me. And her.
I won't. Goodnight, {a}. Goodnight, core.
Goodnight. Mind the cart on your way out.
Night. She says goodnight too.
My plants are doing very well, actually. The tomatoes especially.
For the record, my basil is thriving. Because I talk to it.
Because you talk to them.
So you admit it works.
... I walked into that.
I hate you a little.
It's a matter-antimatter reaction chamber, {a}.
It's a machine. It doesn't know you're there.
I know what it is. It's also the heart of the ship.
I know. And you talk to your plants.
That's different. The plants are alive.
That's different. Plants grow.
She keeps a hundred and forty-one people alive. That counts for something.
She's the reason the plants are alive.
Come on, sweetheart. Just a little steadier. There you go.
Easy, now. Easy. Nobody's asking you to go anywhere.
Morning, you. Let's see how you slept.
Are you... talking to the warp core?
Who are you talking to?
Rhel does it. It's catching.
Yes. Don't tell anyone.
The chief says she listens. I'm not sure he's wrong.
The chief sat up with her all night on the ninth. Talked the whole time.
You know Rhel talked her through the ninth? Out loud, all night.
What did he say?
Was it working?
I don't know. It was in Bajoran. But she stabilised at dawn.
Prayers, I think. Or insults. Hard to tell with Bajoran.
... All right. That's a little bit lovely.
Okay. That's nice. I admit it.
Can I say something to her?
Can I try?
Go on. She likes new voices.
Go ahead. Be polite.
Hi. Thank you for the lights. And the air. And the transporter.
Hello. You're doing very well. We're proud of you.
Thanks for everything. Please don't explode.
See? She's steadier already.
Look at that. Point oh one better.
That's a coincidence.
... Is it?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_10: Um. {a}. Where's the crate of seals?
Wait. Where did the seals go?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_12: How is the crate still up there?
The crate's still on the ceiling.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_13: It had its own lift plate. Of course it did.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_14: I'll get us both a coffee.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_1_: Could we just... tap it down? With the spanner?
What if I throw a coil of cable over it and pull?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_3_: It's coming down! It's... going sideways.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_5_: Got it. Got it. We're fine.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_6_: Excellent. Put it in the log as routine.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_8_: And the dial. Somebody please tape an arrow on the dial.
Label the dial. In big letters. UP means DOWN.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_fix_9_: I'll do it now. With the red tape.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_ladder: The ladder is on the cart.
We put the ladder on the cart.
Why is the ladder on the cart?
Who put the ladder on the cart?
To reach the cart. Before. When it first did this.
For exactly this situation, which has happened before.
So we need a ladder to reach the ladder.
This is a very good system.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_rhel_1: What if the chief comes in?
Rhel will be here in ten minutes.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_rhel_2: Then we tell him it's a test of the ceiling clearance.
Then we salute the cart and hope he doesn't look up.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_rhel_4: He'll look up, sigh, and go back to talking to the core.
He'll look up and say, in Bajoran, something I won't translate.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_start_: Why is the antigrav cart floating by the ceiling?
Has anyone seen the antigrav cart? It was here a minute ago.
Somebody set the lift to maximum. With a crate of spare seals on it.
It's stuck on maximum. Again. I told them the dial is backwards.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_wait_1: It'll drift down when the charge runs out. About two hours.
The field decays. Give it a couple of hours.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_wait_3: Not under it. Never stand under it. Learn from the ensign.
Beside it. Not under. Ask Ensign Haddad why not under.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_cart_wait_5: He's fine. It was a crate of socks. He has a lovely story now.
Fine. Mild bruise. He tells it at every meal.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_acces: Say it, then. You've been circling it for months.
Go on. You're going to say the thing.
It needed command codes and an engineer's hands. Both.
Whoever did it had the codes, and knew exactly where to put them.
That's forty people. Fifty, counting the ones who shouldn't have them.
That's most of this room, {a}. And half the bridge.
I know. I'm on the list. So are you.
I'm aware. I'm on that list. You're on that list.
So is the chief. And Rhel would sooner lose an arm.
So is Rhel, and he'd sooner cut off his own hand.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_close: For what it's worth, the chief's rebuilt every lockout since. Twice.
For what it's worth, nobody's getting into those drives that way again.
Rebuilt them, sure. Nothing left behind them to protect.
Good. Shame there's nothing left behind them to steal.
There's the core. There's the transporter. There's all of you.
There's plenty left, {a}. Air. Light. The pads. Each other.
Carry on. And lock your consoles when you step away.
Back to it. And lock your stations, both of you. Every time.
Since the ninth, every single time.
Good. I'll be on the rounds. Try to talk about something nicer.
Right. Rounds. Talk about the weather. Oh wait, we haven't got any.
We'll talk about the galley menu.
We'll argue about Grieg's stew instead.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_hard_: What I can tell you: it was inside, it was fast, and it was careful.
It was done by somebody who could walk in here without anybody blinking.
Yes. Which is why I'm polite to everybody in this room.
Which is why I don't finish that sentence out loud.
Wonderful. I'll sleep like a baby.
Security. We're a delight at parties.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_kind_: Look. I know it'd be easier if it was somebody. A face.
Listen. A name would feel better. I know it would.
But a wrong name is worse than none. There's a hundred and forty-one of us
But a wrong name is worse than no name. We are a hundred and forty-one
on a ship that can't leave. We don't get to be wrong about each other.
people who can't leave. We don't get to be wrong about each other.
Nobody's accusing anyone, {c}. We're just tired.
We're not pointing fingers. We're just very, very tired.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_logs_: Did security ever get anywhere with the access logs?
What happened with the access logs? Anyone ever say?
The logs are clean. That's the part I can't get past.
Clean. Perfectly clean. Nobody's logs are that clean.
Clean meaning nothing happened, or clean meaning scrubbed?
Clean how? Clean like nobody touched them, or clean like somebody did?
Clean meaning every entry is where it should be, and the ship still died.
Clean like somebody tidied up after themselves and put the chairs back.
That's worse. I think that's worse.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_okafo: What about the Intelligence liaison? Okafor?
People keep saying Okafor's name. Quietly.
People say a lot of things quietly. It's that kind of year.
Cmdr. Okafor has been more help than you'd think. That's all I'll say.
He does look like a man who hasn't slept since February.
He's always in the mess at three in the morning. Staring at tea.
So does the Captain. So do you. Drop it.
So do most of us. Let it go.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_rhel_: You've seen the chief when somebody brings it up.
You know Rhel took it personally.
He went white. Didn't say a word for a full minute.
He rebuilt a panel so hard he cracked the housing.
It's his ship. Somebody reached into his ship and broke it.
It's his engine. Somebody walked in here and did that to it.
He still checks the intermix seals by hand. Every shift. Himself.
He sleeps down here half the week. Says the core gets lonely.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_secur: Is this the February meeting? Nobody sent me the agenda.
You two talking about the ninth again? I could hear you from the lift.
Evening. Are we solving the sabotage? I'll take notes.
Just wondering if your people ever got a name.
Just wondering who security's looking at these days.
If we had a name, you'd know. They'd be in the brig.
Nobody. Which is not quite the same as nothing.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_start: Ninth of February. I still run it back in my head every shift.
Five months, and I still dream about the ninth of February.
I pulled the February logs again last night. Don't look at me like that.
You'll wear a groove in your brain.
Warp and impulse, inside ninety seconds, and every lockout was ours.
Both drives, ninety seconds apart. From in here. From this room.
I know. I was under the port console when the board went red.
I remember. I spilled a whole mug of tea on the systems display.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_ninth_watch: You had the watch that night, didn't you?
You were on gamma, weren't you?
Gamma shift. I was eating a sandwich when it went.
I had the watch. Watched the board go red, left to right, like a wave.
That isn't on you. Nobody thinks it is.
Nobody blames the watch, {a}. Nobody ever has.
I know. Most days I even believe it.
Tren says the same thing. I'm working on it. Slowly.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_the_one_that_wo: So. Transporter perfect, impulse welded.
So we can beam, and we can't move.
We can beam. We keep beaming.
We work with what they left us.
Fused like a surge would fuse them?
That's not a normal failure.
A surge burns. This is too neat. Every regulator at the same weld point.
A surge would take one, maybe two. This took all six, the same way.
That's horrible.
So it was done on purpose. Precisely.
I'm not saying anything. I'm describing a regulator.
I'm just an engineer describing a part. Draw your own conclusions.
Thank the Prophets for the transporter. The chief says so daily.
Without it we'd be a very well-lit tomb.
Without it nobody gets beamed up. No ensigns. No crystals.
No survivors, no dilithium, no Shepard. Nothing.
I polish the pads myself on Sundays.
I think about that a lot.
What about the shuttle? Could the shuttle's parts fit?
Could we strip something out of Shepard's shuttle?
Wrong scale. Her impulse is a toy next to ours.
Maybe the alloy, maybe. I asked. Rhel said not yet.
Not yet is better than no.
I'll take not yet.
Meanwhile, the impulse manifold.
Want to hear about the impulse manifold?
Speaking of dead, I opened the impulse manifold again.
Must I?
No. Yes. Go on.
Six regulators. All six fused. Not burned. Fused. Welded solid.
The flow regulators are fused into the housing. Like they were cast there.
Can they be cut out?
Can you replace them?
I could cut them out. I've nothing to put back. They need a starbase.
We'd need to fabricate new ones, and the replicator can't do that alloy.
The pad crew asked me to thank you, by the way. For the last check.
Kess says the pads have never run cleaner. That's you lot.
It's not us. It's her. She was built right. We just keep her dusted.
We barely touch them. They just work. They've always just worked.
Every survivor that comes up comes up through those coils.
Every ensign they bring up, every crystal. All through those pads.
Somebody down there's been sending them. Nobody knows who.
And whoever's down there marking them. We don't know who that is.
Then whoever it is, I hope they know we're grateful.
I hope they're eating well. I hope they're safe.
Transporter's green on every channel. Again.
Transporter room ran a full check. Perfect. Every buffer, every coil.
Guess what's still working perfectly.
Of course it is.
The transporter. It's always the transporter.
The one thing we can't fly with, and it runs like the day it was built.
Warp dead, impulse dead, and the transporter's never been happier.
Doesn't that bother you?
You don't find that odd?
Every day. They took the drives and left the lifeline.
Constantly. Whoever did the ninth knew exactly which to leave alone.
Or they missed it.
Or they didn't care about it.
Nobody who hits warp and impulse in ninety seconds misses the transporter.
Nobody that careful misses anything.
Back to it. The regulators won't un-weld themselves.
I'll draw up the fabrication specs anyway. Someday.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_bot: The thing is, they're both right.
They're both good. That's the problem.
They are. K'teral's found three faults nobody else would.
K'teral found the cracked housing on the aft injector by kicking it.
And Taval found the drift in the core readings before anyone.
And Taval's numbers are why we're still lit.
Then lock them in a room together.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_chi: He listened to both of them for ten minutes without moving.
He let them go for a full shift. Then he stood up.
He said: K'teral, you'll overdrive the spare. Taval, you'll log every number.
He said they'd do it together. Her way, his notes.
That's the most Bajoran solution I've ever heard.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_end: They've been in the forward bay for four hours.
K'teral laughed. Taval raised an eyebrow.
We're going to get a working injector and a very long report.
Best engineering team on the ship, and they'll never admit it.
I heard she brought him bloodwine to celebrate the first test.
Somebody said he brought her tea. Plomeek. She drank it.
He called it an interesting cultural experience. She called him brave.
She said it tasted of defeat. He said that was the tea's intention.
That's a friendship. That's the start of a real friendship.
Give it a month. They'll be finishing each other's equations.
Right. Back to our own injectors. Nobody overdrive anything.
Back to work. And if you hear a bang, it's science.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_kli: That a system which has never been pushed has never been known.
That you learn nothing from a thing until it screams.
I hate that I agree with her.
No, and Taval said you learn nothing useful from the screaming.
And Taval said you learn it once, and then you need a new injector.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_ref: Are you talking about the injector feud?
Please tell me someone settled the injector argument.
It is unsettled. It may never be settled.
I'd put money on the Klingon. Replicator credits.
My money's on the Vulcan. He never gets tired.
No betting. The chief banned betting after the tribble incident.
Rhel said the next person to run a book cleans the tubes for a month.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_sta: Did you hear Lt. K'teral and Ensign Taval in the forward bay?
Taval and K'teral are at it again. Over the plasma injectors.
You missed it. The Klingon method versus the Vulcan method. Round six.
I heard it from here. Everybody heard it from here.
K'teral wants to overdrive the injector and see what breaks.
K'teral says the injector must be tested in battle. Her words.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_eng_two_schools_vul: Let me guess. Taval had a chart.
Taval said, and I quote: that would be an inefficient use of an injector.
Taval stood very still and said her proposal lacked a hypothesis.
That's the worst thing he could have said.
She said his hypothesis lacked blood.
She said his chart had no honour.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_disaster_cau: I set it in Celsius. The oven's from Shepard's survey. Fahrenheit.
The oven's in Fahrenheit. It's a 1990s oven. I forgot.
So you baked it at four hundred degrees.
Yes. At the temperature of a phaser drill.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_disaster_gri: Grieg is going to be so quiet.
She doesn't shout. She goes quiet and makes you tea. It's worse.
That's why. She'll be kind. I can't bear it.
Make another one. Before she's back.
You've got the dough. Start again.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_disaster_red: What do we do with the black one?
Kurag might want it. He likes things that fought back.
I'll give it a hero's funeral.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_disaster_sal: Can we save any of it?
It's black outside and raw inside.
Put it on the talent night list.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_disaster_smo: The smoke detector's going to go.
I'll wave a tray at it.
If the suppression field goes off, we lose everything in here.
We'd lose a week of dough. Grieg would never forgive me.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_disaster_sta: Is it supposed to be black?
Open the vent. Open the vent!
Don't open the door! Too late.
What did it used to be?
Bread. It was bread. Grieg's starter.
A loaf. It was a loaf.
Grieg's been keeping that starter alive since February.
She calls the starter Gerald. It's older than the sabotage.
No. Gerald's in the jar. We only killed his loaf.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_bargain: He can have the pie if he cleans the vents.
I'll tell him. He'll say cleaning is for targs.
Tell him it's a battle with the ventilation. He'll love it.
Tell him the worms fled. He'll hunt them.
I'll frame it as a hunt.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_complai: What did he write to the captain?
Did he actually file a complaint?
Three pages. I've seen it. It opens with a battle poem.
He filed it. It rhymes. In Klingon.
She wrote back one line. Noted. Eat the pie.
She said she'd review it after the warp core is fixed.
That's the most Captain Vale thing I've ever heard.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_1_1: What does he want me to do? I can't make live gagh.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_1_2: He knows the stasis units have no gagh. Not one.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_2_1: He wants real food. That's all.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_2_2: He wants to eat something honourable.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_3_1: Rokeg blood pie? Grieg did one in May.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_4_1: One pie. In stasis. For emergencies.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fix_5_3: He's been on this ship eight months. It's an emergency.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fury_1_: It wasn't moving. He says it was dead.
He says the worms had no fight in them.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fury_2_: It's replicated. It doesn't move. It can't.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fury_3_: He said that is exactly the problem. At volume.
He called it the gagh of a coward.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_fury_5_: He's in the lounge telling everybody.
He's writing a complaint to Vale.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_grieg_1: Grieg will want it signed for. In triplicate.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_grieg_2: Tell her it's morale. She likes morale.
She'll say yes. She likes him.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_grieg_3: She does. He's the only one who eats her boiled greens.
He brought her a bat'leth when her oven broke. To fix it with.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_pie_1_1: I'm warming the pie. Real heat. Not the replicator.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_pie_1_2: Oven's on. Twenty minutes. Tell him to come hungry.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_pie_2_1: Thank you, {cook}. You've saved a man's honour.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_pie_4_2: It's rokeg blood pie. You don't want any.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_start_1: I need a word about the gagh.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_start_2: Oh no. What happened this time?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_start_3: He ordered gagh. The replicator made gagh.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_gagh_thrown_: Is it true he threw the plate?
Into the replicator. From the door.
The replicator's fine. The worms are in the ventilation.
Nothing broke. Deck crew are cleaning worms off the bulkhead.
Oh, that's going to smell by morning.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_argue_: Name one thing on this ship that tastes better than leola.
Anything. The ration packs. The soap.
The cobbler pack. The recycled water.
I've had the leola. I can extrapolate.
You two do this every time he cooks.
And every week {a} eats a bowl.
And every week you finish it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_defend: It's earthy. It's honest. It's a whole root.
It tastes like wet soil that's angry with you.
Have you had it with chadre'kab?
You haven't had it done properly.
He does it properly. That's the problem. It tastes more of leola.
Properly is worse. Properly is more leola.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_eat_1_: Here. Say something nice to him when you see him.
Bowl. Say thank you to Tessik, mind.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_eat_2_: It's awful. I'm going to finish it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_eat_4_: Don't tell him I said that.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_spice_: Ask him to go easy on the spice.
He puts pepper in it, you know.
He puts Talaxian pepper in everything. It's his signature.
He says pepper makes leola forgive you.
It makes you forget the leola. For about a minute.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_start_: Is that leola root? Is Tessik cooking again?
I can smell leola from the corridor.
Tessik's leola stew. He asked for the galley for an hour.
Crewman Tessik is making leola. For everybody. Whether we want it or not.
Don't be rude. He means well.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_tape_1: Shepard's got a tape. Ninety-Nine Things To Do With Leola Root.
Did you know there's a whole tape about leola? Ninety-nine recipes.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_tape_3: Somebody watched it. Around thing sixty the chef stops pretending.
They said he starts talking about home and how far away it is.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_tape_4: That's the saddest cooking show I've ever heard of.
So even the chef hates leola.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_tape_5: He gets back to it. Thing sixty-one.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_leola_tessik: Why does Tessik do it? Nobody asks for it.
Why does he keep making it?
Because he's the only Talaxian on the ship. It's home.
Because it's the only thing that tastes like his mother's kitchen.
And because it's stasis-stable. Leola keeps forever.
And leola keeps. It's practically indestructible.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_bowl: Here. Real, from stasis. Don't argue.
Here's a bowl. The real one.
I said I would take the replicated.
I asked for the replicator one.
You also said it lets you think. You look like you need to think.
You've been on shift sixteen hours. Eat the soup.
It is exactly as bland as it should be.
It tastes like home. In a very small way.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_c_as: I've never known what plomeek is.
I always thought it was a colour.
A root vegetable. Vulcan. Grown in the desert near ShiKahr.
A soup. Orange. Served at breakfast, with no garnish.
Where I grew up, at every breakfast.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_expl: The pattern overseasons it. It is meant to be bland.
The replicator adds salt. There is no salt in plomeek.
It is meant to be quiet. It lets you think.
It is not meant to taste of anything in particular. That is the point.
That's the most Vulcan thing I've ever heard.
You're describing a soup that's trying not to be a soup.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_quie: Do you need quiet? More than usual, I mean?
One hundred and forty-one people, grieving at once. It is loud.
The ship is anxious. Even when nobody speaks, it is loud.
You are not bad. You are frightened. It is reasonable.
It is not a criticism. It is a very human ship right now.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_reci: Can you tell me how to make it? From scratch?
The root. Water. Heat. Time. Nothing else.
Where do I get the root?
Nowhere near here. But there is a root on the surface. A parsnip.
There are roots in Shepard's samples that are close.
A parsnip. You'd eat parsnip soup?
It would be imprecise. I would eat it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_star: Excuse me. I would like plomeek soup.
Real, from stasis, or the replicator?
Real. The replicated version is inaccurate.
What's wrong with the replicated one?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_plomeek_stoc: We have four bowls in stasis. That's the whole supply.
Three portions left. Then it's replicator or nothing.
So few. There are eight Vulcans aboard.
I know. I've been saving them.
Today is not a bad day. I will have the replicator version.
Then I will not take one. Someone may need it more.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_stasis_count: Log it. Seal them.
Close them up. Keep the cold in.
Sealed.
Units sealed. Power's good.
Thanks, both. Don't tell anyone about the trifle.
Good work. I'll give Grieg the numbers.
What trifle?
My lips are sealed.
The transporter's still bringing things up.
We have options.
And people.
People too. Idris came up last week.
People first. Tins second. That's the order.
People matter more than peaches.
Obviously.
Of course.
Right. Maths. A hundred and forty-one crew.
Right. The sums.
Three meals a day. Replicator does two. The galley does one.
Two replicated meals a day, one real meal a week each.
At this rate, real food lasts till...
How long?
October, if nobody has a birthday.
Till winter. If we're careful.
And after that?
Then what?
Replicator only. Unless someone brings food up from the surface.
Then we need the transporter room to beam up tins.
Unit one. Forty ration packs. Four plomeek. Six hasperat.
Unit one. Thirty-eight packs, three plomeek, and the rokeg pie.
The rokeg pie? Still?
Kurag hasn't found it?
It's labelled cleaning supplies.
Grieg hid it under the cabbages.
Clever.
Good.
So we eat ration packs till Christmas.
Replicated Christmas.
Grieg will do a real Christmas. She'll find a way.
She's saving something. She won't say what.
She is. I've seen the list. It's got a trifle on it.
Unit one, back left. I didn't see it. Neither did you.
Stasis count. Everybody quiet.
Inventory time. Grieg wants numbers.
Right. Count with me, {cook}.
Unit one. Open.
Unit one. Here we go.
Read it out.
Numbers.
Unit three. Mostly surface food. From the beam-downs.
Unit three. Tins. From down there.
What kind?
Label?
Beans. Soup. Peaches in syrup. The labels are 1993.
Canned peaches. Canned corn. A tin that says spam.
Is it safe?
It's four hundred years old.
It's from their 1993. It's about six months old.
It's their year. Not ours. It's fine.
Unit two. Tubers. Andorian. Nine. Oskoid, fourteen.
Unit two. Oskoid. Lots of oskoid. Nobody eats the oskoid.
Why is there so much oskoid?
We've got more oskoid than people.
The Betazoids are too polite to say they don't like it.
Somebody ordered it by the crate in 2433.
Jumja sticks, twenty. Chadre'kab, four.
And three wing-slug rolls.
Wing-slug? We don't have any Orions.
Who's the wing-slug for?
Nobody knows. They've been there since the shakedown.
Rhel. He claims it's for a bet.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_washing_up_d: Stack them. Grieg likes them stacked by size.
Grieg sorts them by colour. Don't mess it up.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_washing_up_h: What was your kitchen like? At home.
Tell me about your kitchen. The one you miss.
Small. Blue tiles. A window over the sink onto a lemon tree.
A station galley on Starbase 12. No window. I loved it anyway.
My dad's kitchen in Nairobi. There was always a radio on.
That sounds like a good place to be.
I did the dishes there every night. Looking out.
That's why I don't mind this. It's the same job.
Well. Look out of this one.
Our window's got a whole planet.
It's not the same. But it'll do.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_washing_up_k: You know what helps me? Doing dishes.
This helps. Stupid, but it does.
They get clean. You can see it. There's not much else like that.
You start with dirty and you end with clean. It's a whole story.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_washing_up_p: This one's from Shepard's lot. It has a flower on it.
Look at this. A cup with a cartoon on it.
Careful. Those are from 1993. Real ceramic.
I think it's a cultural artefact now.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_washing_up_s: That's the verse. There's no more.
Do it again at talent night.
Why aren't we just putting these in the recycler?
Why do we even wash these? Couldn't we recycle them?
Recycling costs power. Water's free. Grieg's rules.
Every plate we recycle is a gram of matter we don't get back.
I know. I was asking the universe.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_galley_washing_up_t: You all right? You've been quiet.
I'm all right. I miss my own kitchen.
Just the planet. You look out the window and remember.
I was on the sensor rota. Counting nothing.
My sister's wedding was last week. I think. I did the maths.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_chea: Wait. Where did you get that money?
The bank gave it to me.
I'm the banker. Bankers get money.
You can't be the banker and a player.
That's how it's done in 1993. I checked with Shepard.
Shepard said everybody cheats at this game. Everybody.
She absolutely did not say that.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_ches: We should have played three-dimensional chess.
Next time, kal-toh. Something with rules that make sense.
I don't lose at chess, I'm strategic in defeat.
Four hundred games since February. You've won nine.
You've won eleven games in eight months.
Eleven. That's a lot. That's a streak.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_end_: That's it. I'm out. You've taken everything.
I own a railway and nothing else.
I'm sorry. Would you like to rent the water company?
It's just business, {a}. Pay your rent.
I hate this game and I love it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_game: Fine. I'll buy the green one.
I'll put a little house on it.
You can't afford the green one.
You can't afford the blue one.
I can if I mortgage the railway.
I'll sell you the water company.
The water company is critical infrastructure.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_jail: You landed on jail. Go directly to jail.
It doesn't say. You just go.
This game has no legal system.
I'm appealing to a Federation magistrate.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_star: Are you going to move or are you asleep?
Don't rush me. Strategy takes time.
You've been thinking for six minutes.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_tidy: Pack it carefully. It's four hundred years old.
Under the bunk. I saw it roll.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_board_game_what: Remind me what this game is even about.
It's from Shepard's shuttle. A 1990s game. You buy streets.
You buy property. You charge rent. You bankrupt your friends.
That's the most un-Federation thing I've ever heard.
Shepard says it's a cultural artefact. The paper money is real paper.
She lent it for research. It's research, {b}.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_bed_: I think I could sleep now.
Try. Close your eyes and count something.
Same time tomorrow if it doesn't work?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_coun: I've been counting the panels on the ceiling.
Forty-four. Then I counted them again in Bajoran. Still forty-four.
Forty-four. They haven't changed since February.
Same ceiling. Same planet. Same forty-four.
I've named some of them too.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_star: Oh. Sorry. I didn't think anyone was up.
It's oh-three-hundred. What are you doing up?
I've been lying there listening to the air recyclers.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_stor: I used to sleep with a recording of rain on. My mother's porch.
When I can't sleep I plan what I'll eat when we get home.
I read old duty rosters. Boring enough to put anybody under.
Everything. Pancakes. A whole lake of pancakes.
Every time. Twenty minutes in and I'm gone.
Rain works. I just can't find the file.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_talk: Do you think we'll ever get home?
Honestly, do you think they'll find us?
I think Rhel will get the engines back, or somebody will come.
I think so. I have to think so.
Yes. Starfleet loses people. Starfleet also looks for them.
Nobody knows we're here. That's the thing.
They don't know where we are.
Not yet. The captain's still transmitting. Every day.
Somebody will notice a science ship never came home.
I needed to hear someone say it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_tea_: Want tea? There's a replicator in the corridor.
It's not my turn on the replicator.
I've got two minutes left. Earl Grey?
Careful. The replicator makes it too hot.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_tren: Maybe mention it to the counselor?
She's so busy. Everybody's in her office.
That's her job. She'd want to know.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_cant_sleep_why_: I keep thinking about the ninth of February.
I dream about the surface. I've never been down there.
The sound when the warp field dropped. I remember it too.
You mean the jolt. I was in the shower.
I dream about it too. Everyone does, I think.
I was on the bridge when the board went red. All of it at once.
I heard Rhel on the comm. I've never heard him like that.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_bribe: I'll make a deal. You go, I'll give you my holodeck slot.
Go, and I'll do your laundry for a week.
Your holodeck slot? The Tuesday one?
The Tuesday one. Two in the morning.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_excus: I'm busy. I've got to calibrate the sensor array.
I've got a report due. For Rhel.
The sensor array's been calibrated for a week.
Your locker has three things in it.
I'm not hiding. I'm avoiding. There's a difference.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_fear_: If I start talking, I don't know if I'll stop.
If I say it out loud it's real.
That nobody's coming. That we're stuck here. Forever, maybe.
That I watched the county die and I felt nothing. Then everything.
That's a lot to carry on your own.
You know the captain goes? Every week.
Even Vale sees her, I heard.
Tuesday mornings. She doesn't hide it. She says it's maintenance.
She told the senior staff. She said if she can, we can.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_go_2_: Want me to come with you? To the door?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_go_5_: You're a good friend. Annoying, but good.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_hones: I don't want to talk about it. That's the whole problem.
I don't know what to say to her. I'm fine. I'm just tired.
You don't have to know. That's her job.
She'll read my mind anyway. She's Betazoid.
Then you've got nothing to hide.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_start: Aren't you supposed to be somewhere?
Don't you have the counselor at ten?
It's ten past. Aren't you due at Tren's?
Tren's going to come looking for you.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_counselor_went_: It helped. She doesn't make you talk about anything you don't want.
She mostly let me sit. She made tea. It was fine.
My dog. For forty minutes. I cried about my dog.
Oskoid. She's the only one who likes the oskoid. We bonded.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_done_3: You'll walk. You'll complain, but you'll walk.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_join_3: I've been sitting at a console for eight months. My back's a disaster.
I'm not letting you get fitter than me.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_mokbar: Have you seen the mok'bara tape on Shepard's shelf?
Shepard's got a tape of Klingon mok'bara. Taught reluctantly.
The instructor hates doing it. He keeps sighing. It's great.
The teacher doesn't want to be there. You learn a lot anyway.
You look like a Klingon who's very tired.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_run_3_: Ten laps. The corridor's about a hundred metres round.
Until one of us falls over.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_run_4_: The corridor that's full of people?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_run_5_: Everybody runs laps. th'Zoran does forty before breakfast.
Security does it every morning. Just shout lift ahead.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_start_: Twelve more. Come on, twelve more.
You're doing push-ups in the corridor.
Is this what you do all day?
Why are you on the floor?
The gym's booked. Security's got it.
The gym's full. The corridor isn't.
People have to step over you.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_stretc: Stretch first. Or tomorrow you'll be walking like Kurag after gagh night.
Stretch. You'll thank me in the morning.
I'm not stretching. Stretching is for Vulcans.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_why_1_: You're doing this every day now.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_why_2_: It helps me sleep. Nothing else does.
I need to be ready. For if they need people down there.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_exercise_why_4_: Somebody might have to. If more of the eleven turn up.
If they ask for volunteers, I want to be fit enough.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_friend_returns_: Are you hungry? You must be hungry.
Starving. I've been dreaming about plomeek soup. And I hate plomeek.
I'd eat a ration pack. I'd eat two.
I'll get you a jumja stick. I've been saving one.
You don't have to do that.
I haven't had a proper wash in a week. Consider yourself warned.
Is that who I think it is?
Did the others make it up?
Some. Idris is up. Tomas came up.
They'll come up. They're tougher than me.
Then we keep looking. That's all.
Your bunk's still there. Nobody touched it.
Your quarters are how you left them.
We weren't going to give it away.
Come on. Food. Then sleep. Then more food.
When did you get up here?
How long have you been aboard?
This morning. Sickbay only just let me go.
What was it like down there?
Where were you all this time?
I don't want to talk about most of it. Not yet.
Hiding. In a school, then a farmhouse.
That's fine. You don't have to.
I ate a lot of tinned peaches.
There were a lot of tinned beans.
We have tinned peaches up here too. You're going to laugh.
You'll never want a peach again.
Have you talked to the counselor?
Tomorrow. She put me in for tomorrow.
Good. Go. Even if you don't want to.
How did you get up? Who found you?
I don't know. Somebody set a beacon. I never saw them.
Somebody tagged me for transport. I don't know who.
The transporter room says that about everyone.
Whoever it is, I owe them.
I'd like to buy them a drink.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_bunk_1_1: She made it before she beamed down. Corners like a cadet.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_bunk_1_2: She left it made. Hospital corners. She was so proud of those.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_bunk_2_1: She was the only one on the deck who did that.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_bunk_3_1: Nobody's touched it. Nobody wants to be the one.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_bunk_3_2: The quartermaster asked if they could reassign it. I said no.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_go_1_1: Come on. Let's get some tea.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_go_1_3: Grieg's doing bread. Maren loved bread day.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_go_2_1: Let me fix the corner first.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_hope_1_1: People are still coming up, you know.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_hope_2_1: I know. Idris. Tomas. Every one makes me think it'll be her next.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_hope_2_2: I know. Every time the transporter room calls, I think it's her.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_hope_5_1: Then we'll sit here. Like this. And remember her right.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_hope_5_2: Then we'll miss her properly. Together. Not on our own.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_memory_1_: Do you remember when she put the geology samples in the fridge?
She sang in the corridor. Badly. Every morning.
She used to leave notes on the replicator. Little jokes.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_memory_2_: The ones labelled not food, trust me?
I've still got one. It says ration your laughter.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_memory_3_: She was so excited to go down. She'd been reading about rivers.
She wanted to see the limestone. The caves. She talked about it for weeks.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_memory_5_: She chose to stay. For the work.
She wanted to finish the survey.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_memory_6_: She did. She knew what she was doing.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_report_1_: I read her last field report. The one from the ninth of February.
I found her last report in the survey files. From before.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_report_3_: Water tables. Karst. Three pages on one cave. She was so happy.
Soil samples. And a note that the farmers waved at the shuttle site.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_report_5_: She signed off with see you Thursday.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_report_6_: We'll keep it. For when she comes up to finish it.
Save it. Somebody should finish it. With her name first.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_sit_1_1: Can we just sit for a bit?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_sit_3_1: She'd hate this. Us being sad on her bunk.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_sit_3_2: She'd tell us to get off her bed.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_sit_4_2: She'd say we're ruining the corners.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_start_2_1: I know. I'm not moving anything.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_grief_start_2_3: I come in here sometimes. Is that strange?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_comp: Could you practise somewhere else? Just sometimes?
I'm on alpha shift. I sleep at twenty-one hundred.
The cargo bay. Nobody's in there. Great acoustics.
Engineering. Rhel wouldn't notice. The warp core is louder.
Rhel talks to the warp core. He'd think I was answering.
I'll try the cargo bay. Sorry.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_deal: Fine. One lesson. And you practise before twenty hundred.
I'll give you a lesson on one condition. Not after twenty hundred.
And I'm coming on Friday. Front row.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_play: The first three notes were lovely.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_star: Is something wrong with the air recycler?
It sounds like the plasma conduits on Deck 5.
It's new. I'm new at it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_tale: I'm on the talent night list.
Four days. I can learn one song in four days.
It's an old Earth thing. It has a lot of high notes.
The one from Shepard's tape. The one they played at the end.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_tips: Try breathing from lower down. Like singing.
You're biting it. Relax your mouth.
I played the oboe for ten years. At school.
My brother played. In the Academy band.
Because I wanted to see how long you'd last.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_instrument_why_: When did you take this up?
March. I needed something to do that wasn't worrying.
After February. The counselor said to get a hobby.
And you picked the loudest instrument aboard.
Tren suggested knitting. I got ambitious.
She suggested a hobby. She did not specify quiet.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_comprom: Right. Your side, your posters. My side stays grey.
Deal. Two on your wall, none on mine.
You're going to crack. I know you are.
Wait till you wake up and see the kitten.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_end_it_: Where's the tape? Shepard gave me tape.
Do not put a hole in the bulkhead.
I would never damage the Adirondack.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_kitten_: Fine. The kitten can go above my bunk.
Don't make a thing of it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_more_3_: A band. A film. A beach. And a kitten on a branch.
A film. A car. And one that just says hang in there.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_more_5_: It's hanging on to a branch. It's very inspiring.
It means hold on. Keep going. It's for us, really.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_shuttle: It's like Lieutenant Shepard's shuttle. She has one.
Shepard's shuttle has a refrigerator and a lamp. It's a museum.
Shepard's shuttle is a field station. This is our quarters.
It makes it feel like a teenager's bedroom.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_start_1: Don't say anything yet. Just look at it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_start_2: Why is there a paper rectangle on our wall?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_start_3: It's a poster. From the surface.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_start_4: Is that a man with a guitar on fire?
Why is it a picture of a car?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_taste_1: Where did you even get it?
How did you get it up here?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_taste_2: The last beam-up. It was in a shop window. I asked the transporter room.
Shepard had spares. She said take one, it's good for morale.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_taste_3: Did it have a price on it?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_taste_4: It says sale. Sale was their word.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_taste_5: You'd pay four whole dollars for that?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_posters_taste_6: I have no idea what a dollar is.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_co: Deal. Twenty minutes each. Mornings mine, evenings yours.
Here's the deal. You get evenings. I get mornings.
Your time, your teeth. Just put it back to medium after.
Maximum on your time. Medium on mine. Reset it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_ki: You can have the forty minutes.
Take the forty. I'll use Deck 3's.
No, you're right. I'll time it.
I'll find somewhere else to hide.
Or hide in here with the lights off and I'll pretend I'm asleep.
There's the observation lounge at night. Nobody's there after two.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_la: I'm putting a label on the panel.
I'll write it on the wall.
I want it witnessed. By a Vulcan.
She'd make us fill in a transporter form.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_qu: Honestly? I go in there to sit.
Everything. The window. The sensor map. The news that isn't news.
Nobody can find you in a sonic shower. It's the only door that locks.
It's fine. It's just... it hums. It drowns things out.
It's loud in the right way.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_se: And you left it on your setting again. Maximum.
Maximum is the only setting that does anything.
Maximum is how it's meant to be.
Maximum makes my teeth hum for an hour.
I came out of it hearing colours.
That's how you know you're clean.
That's how you know it's working.
That's how you know you've been to a rock concert.
I don't want to be clean at a molecular level. Just clean.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_st: You were in the sonic shower for forty minutes.
