Did you fall asleep in the shower again?
I was thinking. It's the only quiet place on the ship.
I timed it. I had a PADD.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_sonic_shower_wa: I want a real shower. With water. Just once.
Everyone wants a water shower. There's a rota.
Water showers are Thursday. Four minutes.
Four minutes. I have hair, {a}. I have a lot of hair.
Four minutes isn't a shower. It's a rinse with ambition.
Shepard had a bath in her shuttle. A real bathtub.
You know the Adirondack has one bathtub? In the captain's quarters.
I didn't need to know that.
And does Vale ever use it?
Never. She sleeps four hours and showers sonic like the rest of us.
Rumour says she keeps plants in it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_unsent_letter_c: I wrote about June. About watching the county on the sensors.
I wrote about the two days. When all the life signs went.
That's a lot to put in a letter.
I don't know how to say it. They were people. Ordinary ones.
The school still had its lights on the first night. I don't know why.
No. Nobody knows how to say it.
I think you should keep it. Maybe not send it. But keep it.
They'd want to know you were all right. And you weren't. That's fine.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_unsent_letter_f: My dad. He reads everything twice.
My grandmother. She still writes on paper.
She'll want to know if I've been eating. Every letter.
He'll check it for spelling. He can't help it.
She'll pin it on the wall and tell her whole school.
Then tell her you've been eating.
I have. Sort of. Leola counts.
I'll get it right for once.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_hab_unsent_letter_l: Put something good in it. There's good stuff too.
Tell them about something funny. Something that happened.
Kurag throwing gagh at a replicator.
The shower treaty on Deck 2. Everyone's heard.

I know. That's half my caseload this week.
I know. Ask me instead of the mess hall. I'm cheaper.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_gr: Let me guess. You've been reading a PADD in the dark.
Let me guess. Four hours of sleep and six cups of coffee.
Is that a guess or did you look at my file?
Three cups. Maybe four. Grieg's rationing the real stuff.
It's a guess. It's always the same guess lately.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_hu: Is that a real thing? A recording of the engines?
Placebo is real too, and it's the cheapest medicine aboard.
Try it. If it doesn't work, it cost you nothing but pride.
Rhel would want to tune it. Properly.
Rhel talks to the real one. Everyone needs a hobby.
Don't tell Rhel I said so, but I'd listen to that recording.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_hy: Here. Mild analgesic, and a little something for the fluids.
Hold still. Analgesic and electrolytes. Neck, please.
Is that from the ration? I don't want to waste one.
Are we allowed to use those on headaches now?
A headache on shift is a mistake waiting to happen.
We ration them. We don't hoard them. There's a difference.
Oh. That's... better. That's much better.
Water. Two litres today, and I will ask.
Drink something that isn't coffee. Please.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_jo: Before you ask: no, I haven't hit my head on anything.
And no, I didn't walk into a bulkhead. Not this time.
That's exactly what people who walk into bulkheads say.
Noted. I'll scan for bulkhead-shaped dents anyway.
... There might have been a door. It didn't open fast enough.
The doors have been sluggish since February. You're not the first.
Engineering rerouted half the door servos. Doors hit everyone now.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_or: Eight hours. That's a medical order, and I'm logging it.
Eight hours tonight. I'm writing it in your file.
What if I just lie there again?
Then you come back and we talk to Tren.
Then you tell Counselor Tren. Tren's better at the lying-there part.
Tren's got half the ship on the list already.
Tren will fit you in. Tren fits everyone in.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_sc: Follow the light. ... Good. Other way.
Hold still. The tricorder doesn't like fidgeting.
Blood pressure's fine. Pupils are fine. You're dehydrated.
No bleed, no pressure, nothing scary. You're just tired and dry.
That's it? I was ready for something dramatic.
Nothing a hypospray and a night's sleep won't fix.
Sorry to disappoint. It's the boring kind of headache.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_sl: How much are you sleeping? Honestly.
When did you last sleep a full cycle?
Four hours. Five, on a good night.
I lie down. That's not the same thing, is it.
The ship's too quiet since the engines went. I keep listening.
Quarters are too quiet. No warp hum. I didn't know I needed it.
You're not the only one. Half the crew misses the hum.
Engineering keeps promising to pipe in a recording. Ask Rhel.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_headache_st: Got a minute? My head's been pounding since yesterday.
Is this a bad time? My head is killing me.
Sit on the biobed. When did it start?
Up on the bed. How long has it been going?
Every third person this week. Sit down, let's see yours.
End of beta shift. Right behind the eyes.
Two days, on and off. Worse in the mornings.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_nightmares_: Thank you. I mean it.
Three nights. Then Tren. Okay.
Thanks. I didn't think I could say it out loud.
You did say it out loud. That's the hard part done.
Come back any time. Night or day.
Sleep well. Or at least, sleep.
It's just stress. Everyone's stressed.
It doesn't matter. I just need to sleep.
It matters to me. I don't hand out sedatives blind.
Humour me. I have to put something in the file.
... All right.
Fine. You'll think it's stupid.
I was in here that night. We had the sensor feed too.
I saw the same feed from here. We had it up on the lab wall.
You did?
Then you know.
I know. I still think about it too.
I do. Some nights I don't sleep either.
What do you do?
How do you manage?
Badly, sometimes. I talk to Anwar. I talk to Tren.
I work. I talk. I let myself be sad about it. That's allowed.
And now you see it when you close your eyes.
And that's what you see at night.
Every night. The readout. The count going down.
Every time. I dream I can stop it if I read faster.
You couldn't have stopped it. Nobody aboard could.
There was nothing any of us could do. Not from up here.
We have transporters. We could have done something.
We had a whole ship. And we watched.
A ship without engines, and an order not to interfere.
We watched because watching was all we were allowed. And able.
I'll give you something mild. Three nights, then we talk.
Here's a mild sedative. Three nights only.
And I'm booking you with Tren. Not optional.
And you're seeing Counselor Tren this week. Doctor's orders.
Tren's booked out for weeks.
Tren has the whole crew on the list.
Then I'll trade. Tren owes me a favour.
Then I'll sit in Tren's doorway until there's a slot.
Observe only. Uxbridge. Miri. I know the file by heart now.
Observe only. That order. I hate that order.
Hate it if you need to. It was argued in good faith.
Careful people wrote it, for good reasons. It still hurts.
They were people down there. Real people.
Every one of those dots was a person. With a name.
They were. That's why it hurts. It's supposed to.
They were. Remember them that way. Not as the readout.
Can you give me something to sleep? Something strong?
I need something to stop the dreams.
Is there anything for nightmares? Anything at all?
Maybe. Tell me what's happening first.
Sit down. Tell me about the dreams.
Sleep aids I have. Tell me why.
I was on the long-range sensors in June. The last week.
I had the science station. The night it started. In June.
I watched the county on the display. The life signs.
I was watching the life signs over the county. All night.
Oh.
I see.
They just... went out. Town by town. Two days.
We watched the numbers go down, and there was nothing to do.
Some of our people were down there. When it happened.
The eleven. Were any of them near the towns?
Some. And some have come up since. Every one is a small miracle.
Some came through. We've got bunks full of proof.
So there's a chance.
Then it wasn't all just... watching.
There's always a chance. That's why the beds stay made.
No. Somebody down there is still answering. We keep listening.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_c: And the regenerator cells?
What about the cells? We're down to nine.
Send them to Engineering. They'll recharge on the core overnight.
Engineering can recharge those. Costs almost nothing.
Almost nothing?
You said almost.
Rhel wants a thank-you. In person. With biscuits.
Almost. Rhel wants the empties labelled. Properly, this time.
Done. I'll bake them myself if I have to.
Fine. Grieg can help with the biscuits.
I'll put it in the schedule.
Right. I'll update the allotment.
I'll send the paperwork.
Thank you. Truly.
Appreciated. Go on, before I ask for more.
Thanks. And come in for your physical, you're overdue.
I'm fine.
... I'm always overdue.
What can we cut?
Where can we trim?
Headaches. No hyposprays for headaches. Tea and bed instead.
The minor stuff. Bruises get the regenerator only. No hypos.
Agreed. Nobody dies of a headache.
Fine. Tell the staff. Tea, water, bed.
And the quartermaster's here. Looking for you.
The quartermaster's at the door. Wants a word.
Doctor. A word about your hours?
Doctor. Got a minute?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_d: Here's my offer. Six hours a month. Cartridges only.
Six hours. We drop the cells. Engineering can recharge those.
Five, and I'll find you a sixth if we have a quiet month.
Five. But if anyone comes up from the surface, I get what I need.
Five and a half, and rescues come first. Always.
Deal. Rescues first. Nobody would say otherwise.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_g: The galley gave up two hours last week. For you.
Grieg already gave up hours. Cooks on real stoves now.
Real bread. The whole crew's grateful.
Grieg is a saint. An actual saint.
Then Medical gives up something too. Fair's fair.
Then we'll match it. Medical isn't special.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_n: How long does that last us?
Six weeks. Eight if nobody spars.
Two months. If nobody else comes up hurt.
And people will come up hurt. That's the point.
Every rescue comes up needing something. We plan for them first.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_q: Every replicator hour is power. Power is dilithium. We can't mine.
Replicator time runs off the core. And the core is all we've got.
And every cartridge is somebody's life.
I understand. But medicine is not optional.
Nobody said it was. I'm saying pick what matters most.
I'm not saying no. I'm saying prioritise.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_r: What would it cost to replicate a batch?
Operations says the medical allotment's already over.
The replicator schedule's full. The quartermaster's been by twice.
You rang? I heard my favourite word.
I was coming to see you anyway. You're over, Doctor.
I was on my way. We need to talk about your replicator hours.
Rhel says the core can take more, if we're careful. Maybe.
Engineering thinks there's slack in the power budget. Rhel's guessing.
Rhel's usually right about that core.
Rhel also talks to it. So.
Rhel also calls it sweetheart. Grain of salt.
Everyone talks to something up here.
I talk to the biobeds. It's fine.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_rationing_s: Inventory's done. You're not going to like it.
Doctor, the monthly count. It's not pretty.
Hypospray cartridges. We need to talk.
I never like it. Go on.
Forty-one full cartridges. Nine regenerator cells.
Forty cartridges and change. And the cells are low.
Speaking of which. Anything from the surface?
Any signal from down there this week?
th'Zoran has the transporter room on watch round the clock.
Nothing new. But the transporter room never sleeps.
Then we keep two biobeds free. Always. Non-negotiable.
Then neither do our beds. One made up, always.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_car: Log it. Exactly as observed. No conclusions.
Into the file. Observed only. Don't speculate on paper.
Nothing? We've got a whole shelf of guesses.
A guess in a file becomes a fact in a week.
Guesses spread faster than anything in that dish.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_clo: The captain has everything we have. Every day.
Vale reads every report. Asks for these ones first.
Shepard's soil samples from March make a decent control.
Lieutenant Shepard's spring baselines are helping, actually.
Good. Use them. Anything from before June is precious.
Then use them. Pre-June baselines are gold.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_des: The swab set that came up with the last ensign. Their gear.
Soil and cloth, from the last rescue. Decontaminated twice.
And it's still showing that pattern?
The folding, and something riding along with it.
Protein structure that shouldn't hold still. And it doesn't.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_doc: The same confusing markers, Doctor. Still.
More of the same. Markers that don't agree with each other.
It reads like two things. Two signatures that shouldn't coexist.
Half of it looks like one thing. The other half, another.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_emh: You've sent these to the Doctor?
All of them. He ran the first ones himself.
Every one. He went very quiet, for a hologram.
That the chemistry is sound. Nothing about where it came from.
He'll vouch for the chemistry. Not much else.
That sounds like him. Careful to the last decimal.
Then that's what goes in the log. Chemistry only.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_rer: Consistent is something. Consistent we can work with.
Consistent is how we'll find it. Keep going.
Stubborn data is still data. Log it, then rest.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_sta: That's the fourth run. Same markers.
Same as yesterday. Same as last week.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_the: Could it be local? A parallel Earth, parallel bugs?
What if it's just native biology? Something endemic?
Earth bugs don't look like this. Nothing on file does.
If it were native we'd have a match in the archives. We don't.
Engineered, then. That's what they say in the mess.
People in the mess say it's a weapon. Section 31.
People in the mess say a lot of things.
I don't do people in the mess. I do data.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_samples_wra: I'll run it once more with the new calibration.
Once more, then I'm going to eat something.
Then we compare with the June set.
I'll pull the June samples out of stasis.
Careful with those. Gloves, both of you.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_ad: ... It may be a little cracked.
Perhaps there is a small crack. A small one.
Tell anyone, and the next match is not a draw.
No sparring for three days. Either of you.
Three days off the mat. Both of you. I mean it.
Three days? Security drills are Thursday.
What are we supposed to do for three days?
Paperwork. Reading. Something that doesn't hit back.
There's a shuttle full of old Earth board games. Try one.
The Earth games? I tried one. There was paper money.
Shepard's shuttle games have no blood in them.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_cl: Go. And no rematch in the corridor.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_kl: And you. You're holding your side.
You're breathing short. Let's have a look at you too.
A Klingon does not come to sickbay for bruises.
It is nothing. A warrior's ache.
Took an elbow in the ribs. I felt it land.
You took my elbow right in the ribs. I heard it.
That was the sound of your technique failing.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_re: On the bed, or I call Lieutenant th'Zoran.
Bed. Now. Or it's light duty for a week.
I would, and I'd enjoy the paperwork.
Try me. I have nothing but time up here.
... Fine. For the record, it does not hurt.
Very well. Scan. You will find nothing.
Keep your wrist straight this time.
I look forward to it. Bring your good wrist.
And report here after. Not the next morning.
And you both come here after. Or before, preferably.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_sc: One cracked rib. Clean, at least.
Lie back. Regenerator, ten minutes. You're not going anywhere.
Ten minutes on the bed. I'm setting it before you make it worse.
Ten minutes. In sickbay. My ancestors weep.
This is how I will be remembered. Lying down.
I'll bring you a blanket. And a story for the mess.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_st: Doc, it's nothing. Just a wrist.
Don't make a fuss. I landed wrong.
Sprained it sparring. My own fault.
You blocked with your wrist. I told you not to.
I said keep the wrist straight. Twice.
Both of you, sit. Who started it?
Let me guess. Holodeck's rationed, so you used the gym.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_tr: No injury, understood. Just for my records. Deep breath in.
Humour me, then. Arms up. All the way.
That noise is called a cracked rib.
Mm-hm. And that was the noise of nothing?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_wh: A draw is what the loser calls it.
I don't care who won. I care who's bleeding.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_sparring_wr: Make a fist for me. Slowly.
That's the one. That's the ow.
Sprain, not a break. The ligament's angry but intact.
Mild sprain. You'll live, and you'll keep the hand.
Arm on the tray. Dermal regenerator, three minutes.
It tickles. Why does it always tickle?
Is it supposed to feel like ants?
It's knitting you back together. Be grateful it only tickles.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_a: It's one week. It's just a stimulant.
Other ships hand them out. It's standard stock.
Just enough to get through. I'm not asking for much.
We're not other ships. We can't replace what we use.
Standard stock is exactly what we don't have.
A tired engineer on a plasma conduit is a hazard, not a hero.
Tired hands make mistakes. In Engineering, mistakes burn.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_b: What about the mild one? The one for night duty?
Negotiating with the CMO's office. Bold.
Half a dose of a bad idea is still a bad idea.
Dr. Anwar would give it to me.
The Doctor would. If I asked properly.
Anwar wrote the policy. The Doctor would recite it back to you.
Anwar wrote the rule. The Doctor would lecture you for an hour.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_c: Since you're here. On the bed. Humour me.
While you're sitting down. Let me look at you.
I'm fine. I came for a hypo, not a physical.
This is a trap, isn't it.
Heart rate's up. Cortisol's through the roof. Eyes like a map.
You're running on adrenaline and replicator coffee. Mostly coffee.
That's just what Engineering looks like now.
Everyone down there looks like this.
Then everyone down there is getting a note from me.
Then I'll be seeing everyone down there. One at a time.
All right. Three days. And sleep.
Fine. You win. Thanks, I think.
I'll tell Rhel it's doctor's orders.
Good. Go on. And eat on your break.
Now go, before I find something else wrong with you.
Tell Rhel. And tell Rhel to come and see me.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_f: ... Fine. I knew you'd say no.
You came anyway. That tells me something.
Because I'm tired, Doc. We're all tired.
I don't know. Hoping, I suppose.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_o: I'm writing to Rhel. Three days of doubles, maximum, then sleep.
Nobody does doubles more than three days running. I'll tell Rhel.
Rhel will complain about you to the warp core.
Good. It'll be the most sensible talk in Engineering.
Let Rhel. The core agrees with me.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_p: I can take it. I've done doubles before.
It is. And you're my patient. So, no.
You did doubles on a ship with a starbase at the end of the week.
Rhel needs you in a year, not just this week.
No. It's true, which is worse.
It isn't supposed to be fair. It's supposed to be right.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_r: Rhel's taking it hard, you know. The sabotage. Personally.
Rhel hasn't slept properly since February either.
I know. Rhel's on my list. Rhel doesn't know it yet.
I know. Rhel's next. Don't say anything.
Good luck. Rhel hides in the Jefferies tubes.
Rhel will say fine. Rhel always says fine.
Everyone here says fine. I have a hypospray for fine.
Then I'll take the tricorder into the tubes.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_s: I need something to keep me up. Double shifts, all week.
Doc, I need a stimulant. Rhel's got us on doubles.
I need a favour. Something to keep me sharp for sixteen hours.
Sit down and tell me why first. Then I'll say no.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_stimulant_w: The plasma manifolds. Rhel wants every conduit rechecked.
We're rebuilding the impulse relays. Again. By hand.
The relays that have been dead since February.
The ones that were sabotaged five months ago?
Rhel says they're one good week from working.
Rhel has said that every week since February.
Rhel says that to the warp core too. It isn't listening either.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_cl: Is that it? Same time next week?
Same time next week. And come in any time before that.
Next week. Or sooner. Sickbay's always open.
Go on. You're doing better than you think.
... Thank you. For all of it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_fo: The food's strange too. Grieg keeps giving me extra.
Petty Officer Grieg keeps slipping me extra bread.
That's how the galley says welcome home.
Take it. Grieg would be offended if you didn't.
I ate from cans for weeks. Cold beans. From a shop shelf.
Down there I ate out of cans. Cold. I keep thinking about it.
Eat slowly. Your stomach's still catching up.
Small meals for now. Your body needs time.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_gu: There were others. We were a team of three, in the valley.
I wasn't alone down there. Not at first.
You don't have to talk about it here.
I read the report. Say as much or as little as you want.
I got a signal out. They didn't. That's the whole story.
I'm here because I was closer to the transmitter. That's it. Luck.
That's not all. You kept yourself alive long enough to call.
Luck, and you kept going. Both things are true.
Somebody beamed me up. I never found out who.
Somebody answered. I don't even know who to thank.
Neither do we, honestly. Somebody's working the surface.
We don't fully know either. Somebody down there keeps finding you.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_ho: The others. Is there any word?
Has anyone else come up? Since me?
Not since you. The beds are ready. They're always ready.
No one new yet. We keep watching. Every shift.
I keep thinking about why we stayed.
We stayed for the fieldwork. It seemed so important.
It was important. None of you did anything wrong.
You stayed to do your jobs. Nobody here blames you. Nobody.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_ph: Arm out. Let's see the cut.
Let me look at your hand. How's it healing?
Clean. Barely a mark. The regenerator did good work.
Healed nicely. Scans are clear. Every one of them.
You're sure? You're sure I'm not... carrying anything?
I'm sure. The Doctor ran the full panel twice. You're clear.
Clear. Anwar checked, the Doctor checked, I checked. Clear.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_qu: Everything smells like nothing up here.
Down there everything smelled like something. Smoke. Rain.
I got used to listening. For anything. It's too quiet up here.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_sl: Some. I wake up at every door.
Three. Maybe. I check the door. I know it's locked. I check anyway.
That's normal, for now. It'll ease.
That's your body keeping watch. It'll learn it can stop.
I can give you something mild, if you want. Your call.
There's a sedative if you want it. No pressure.
Not yet. I want to try without.
Maybe. Not tonight. Maybe next week.
Then the offer stands. Any hour, any night.
That's fine. It's there when you want it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_st: Come in, {ensign}. Just a follow-up today.
Sit wherever you like. This one's routine.
You don't have to keep checking on me.
I do, actually. It's in the rules. And I want to.
Humour me. It's week two. Week two is when things show up.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_survivor_tr: Have you seen Counselor Tren yet?
Twice. Tren's good. I don't say much.
Once. I talked about the weather. For an hour.
The weather's a fine place to start.
That counts. Tren will take whatever you give.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_the_argumen: Bedside manner. His.
Anwar says he used the word terminal on a sprained ankle.
He did not.
He didn't. Did he?
He said it was technically a terminal ligament.
He said it was anatomically accurate. Which it was.
Oh, no.
That poor ensign.
Five replicator credits says round five starts before lunch.
I'll bet you a coffee ration they're at it again by gamma shift.
No bet. Obviously they will be.
You're on. Actually, no. I'd lose.
Remember when Captain Vale came down to referee?
Did you hear the captain had to settle one last week?
The analgesic thing? I heard Vale sat between them.
Vale came down? For an argument about gauze?
Vale listened for ten minutes and said they were both right.
Vale heard them out, said both were right, and left.
That's why the captain's the captain.
Then they argued about which one was more right.
For another hour.
Naturally.
Back to the cabinets, then.
Right. Inventory.
Come on. The biobeds won't calibrate themselves.
After you.
Coming.
Anwar told me once he's the best colleague there's ever been.
Anwar says he's the only one aboard who reads as much as a CMO.
Has anyone told him that?
Don't let him hear that. His ego would need its own deck.
Never. Anwar would rather resign.
Of course not. He'd be insufferable.
He knows anyway. He must.
He knows. He's a hologram, not an idiot.
Was that a laugh? I think Anwar laughed.
Did somebody just laugh in there?
They always end up laughing.
That's how it ends every time. Wait for it.
I think they like it. The arguing.
They'd be lost without each other. You know that.
Opera. He wants to sing to the patients in recovery.
He wants opera in the recovery ward. For morale.
For morale? Whose morale?
Oh, that's not happening.
His, mostly.
Anwar threatened to delete the subroutine. He said try it.
Dosing. The Doctor wants to cut the analgesic ration by ten percent.
Hypospray allocation. The Doctor's built a model. With decimals.
And Anwar?
Let me guess. Anwar says the model doesn't bleed.
Anwar said, and I quote, patients are not spreadsheets.
Anwar says the model forgets that people are people.
The Doctor's not wrong, though. We have to stretch it.
Honestly, they're both right. That's the problem.
Are they still at it?
Is that Anwar and the Doctor in the office again?
Listen. They're arguing again.
Since the start of shift.
For an hour now. Right through the door.
Round three. Maybe four.
What is it this time?
What's the subject today?
Remember when he locked Anwar out of the lab?
Remember the week they didn't speak? In March?
Over the stasis pods. God. Yes.
The whole week. They sent notes through me. I was a courier.
And how did it end?
Who won?
Anwar brought him a medical text he hadn't read. Instant peace.
He apologised with a thirty-page report. Anwar framed the cover.
That's them exactly.
That is the most them thing I've ever heard.
Door's opening. Look busy.
Uh oh. Door. Look like we're working.
I am busy. I'm always busy.
I'm counting regenerator cells. Very busy.
Doctor Anwar. Good shift?
Morning, Doctor. Everything all right in there?
... Smiling. So who won?
... That's a smile. That's either a win or a truce.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_the_author_: The author. As if it were written.
Like somebody wrote it. Like a book.
Or like two people wrote it. That's the bit I can't let go.
A manuscript with two hands in it. That's what he meant, I think.
That's a horrible thought.
Two hands. I'm going to lose sleep over that.
Then don't think it too hard. We don't know. Nobody does.
I'm not saying I know. I'm saying he doesn't guess. Ever.
We should get back.
Right. Biobeds. Somebody might come up tonight.
This stays here.
Not a word in the mess.
Keep it off the record. Please.
Not a word.
Understood. Of course.
It means he's a careful hologram. That's all.
It means he won't sign his name to a guess.
That's not all, and you know it.
You're doing the thing Anwar does. The not-answering.
... Fine.
... All right. Sit down.
And that's related how? To any of this?
Phlox was treating something completely different, surely.
I don't know. I can't see the link. He hasn't said.
Maybe it isn't. I don't know. He won't say yet.
Then why tell me?
So why are we whispering?
Because he looked hopeful. For a hologram. That's all.
Because it's the first time since June he's looked hopeful.
The markers read like one thing and another thing. At once.
Two signatures in one sample. They shouldn't coexist.
The chemistry is real. He could prove every bond.
He can map the chemistry perfectly. That was never the problem.
What he wouldn't say is who made it. Or what.
He wouldn't name a maker. He said the evidence didn't point to one.
Shepard thought it was Section 31.
Everyone thinks it's Section 31. Or the Q theory. Or one of us.

Shepard's a careful person. He still wouldn't sign it.
So there's a counter? A treatment?
Does that mean there's a cure?
It means there's paperwork. Paperwork isn't a cure.
It means there's a note in a file. That's all. For now.
But he's reading it.
But he thinks it's relevant.
He read it twice. He doesn't read things twice.
He hasn't put it down since.
I heard something the Doctor said. To Shepard, on the channel.
There's a line going round. Something the Doctor said.
I can support the chemistry. I cannot support the author.
You mean the chemistry line. I was there.
What did he mean by it?
That's the one. What does it mean?
Commander Okafor came through the lab, after. I saw.
Okafor was here that week too. Reading the reports.
I saw.
Yes.
He looked shaken. Okafor. Shaken.
I've never seen that man look anything. He looked frightened.
Let's not do rumours in sickbay. There's enough going round.
Everybody gets frightened. Even Intelligence. Leave it.
Sorry.
You're right. Sorry.
There's something else. The Doctor's been reading.
Have you seen what the Doctor's pulled out of the archive?
He's always reading.
That's not news. He reads everything.
A medical log. From 2153. Phlox, on the old Enterprise.
Phlox. Denobulan, twenty-second century. A log nobody reads.
Phlox? That's nearly three hundred years old.
Phlox? That's a museum piece.
A note about omicron radiation. A treatment. Filed and forgotten.
Omicron radiation. Phlox used it against something. Once.
Can I ask you something? Off the record.
You were on shift the night of the fourth. In July.
You worked on the surface samples with the Doctor, didn't you.
Depends what it is.
Some of them. Why?
Close the door first.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_transporter: No more test cycles today. I'll tell th'Zoran myself.
You're off the volunteer list for a week.
The lieutenant won't like that.
But they need bodies for the calibration.

A crate of rations. That's actually a good idea.
... Okay. Okay, I think it's passed.
Sorry. Sorry about the basin.
I've seen worse. I've seen worse this week.
Don't apologise. It's a very good basin.
Thanks, Doc. I'll walk slowly.
Right. Slowly. Thanks.
Thanks, {doc}. Sorry again about the basin.
Sit up for five minutes first. Then go.
Walk, don't run. And eat something plain.
Mind the door. The doors are slow.
Old remedy. Ginger. Grieg keeps a real root in the galley.
Go and ask Grieg for ginger tea. The real kind, not replicated.
Real ginger? Grieg will never part with it.
Grieg rations ginger like it's dilithium.
Tell Grieg I sent you. The galley owes me for last month's burn.
Say it's prescribed. It is. I'm prescribing it.

Right now I understand them completely.
Right now I'm on the side of the shuttles.

Then here's the thing they didn't always have.
Antiemetic. Hold still.
Neck. This one is for the nausea.
Oh, that's... the floor has stopped moving.
Better. Much better. Thank you.
You know it's the same molecules, going back where they were?

Tell my inner ear.
My inner ear has filed a complaint.
It's worth it, though. Isn't it? If somebody calls.
I'd do it again. If it helps bring one of the eleven home.
It is. And that's why I want you well for it.
I know. That's why I'd rather you rested than fainted.
Any word? Anyone new come up?
Has anyone... come up lately?
Not this week. We keep the beds made.
Not lately. But the beds are ready. They're always ready.
Were you here for the last pickup? The ensign from the valley?
Were you on shift when the last one came up?
I was. Straight off the pad and onto that bed.
I was. We had the bed ready before the beam finished.
th'Zoran said the lock was thin. Barely a signal.
They said the pattern buffer only just held.
Then calibrate away. Just not on my patients' stomachs.
Which is why I won't stop you testing. Only complain about it.
Pattern integrity's perfect. You're all you.
Scanning... Every molecule present and accounted for.
Then why do I feel like I've been folded?
Then why does the room keep tilting?
Transporter vertigo. Some people just get it.
Your brain didn't like the reassembly. It'll sulk for an hour.
I think I'm going to be sick.
Is there a basin? Asking for me.
Doc. Transporter. Again. Ugh.
Sit. Head down. Breathe through your nose.
Here. Basin. Aim well.
Pad-to-pad test again?
th'Zoran ran another pad-to-pad calibration. I volunteered.
Test cycle. Pad to pad. Three times.
Three times? Why three?
Why are they cycling people at all?
Buffers. th'Zoran wants them perfect for the next pickup.
If anyone signals from down there, it has to work first time.
Fair. Better you than a survivor with a broken leg.
Can't argue. We get one shot at each of them.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_clos: You're done. Clean bill of health.
That's it. See you next year. Or sooner, if you break something.
Thank you, Doctor. Live long and prosper.
I will return in one year. Precisely.
Peace and long life. Mind the door.
I'll hold you to the second.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_joke: I've been told Vulcans do have a sense of humour.
Someone told me Vulcans tell jokes. Very quietly.
I have never told a joke.
Your tricorder is displaying my scan upside down.
Doctor, your regenerator is set to veterinary.
It isn't. It isn't! ... Was that a joke?
... No, it's not. Hang on. Was that...?
I'm writing that down. Box eight. Possible humour detected.
I'm telling the whole ward. Nobody will believe me.
No one will believe you. That is correct.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_medi: You still sit at the observation window?
The view of the planet is conducive to contemplation.
Yes. The planet below is... instructive.
Even after what happened down there?
Especially now. It would be illogical to look away.
Particularly. Looking away would not honour what we saw.
... That's a kind way to put it.
I think that's the right answer.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_mood: And morale? Your own, I mean.

That is not a medical question.
Everyone aboard has morale. Even you.
It's on the form. Box seven.
Then write: acceptable, given the circumstances.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_obse: The sickbay lighting is three percent brighter than regulation.
Your door takes point four seconds longer to open than in March.

Engineering has bigger problems than our door.

Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_scan: Hold still. ... Heart rate's fine. Well. Vulcan fine.
Blood pressure fine. Copper levels fine. Everything's fine.
I could have told you this.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_slee: Vulcans require less sleep than humans.
I meditate. It is more efficient than sleep.
The ship is quieter without the warp drive. It is... noticeable.
The absence of the engines is an unusual variable.
You too? Half the crew says the same thing.
Miss is imprecise. I have registered its absence.
I would not say miss. I would say I notice.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_soup: I have one request. Medical, in nature.
There is one matter. Related to diet.
My replicator ration rarely permits plomeek broth.
The current rations are deficient in plomeek soup.
A plomeek deficiency. Is that a medical condition?
You want a prescription. For soup.
Twice a week would be logical.
I would describe it as a nutritional requirement.
I'll write it up. Soup, twice weekly.
Fine. Two bowls a week. Don't tell anyone I did this.
I will inform no one. It would be illogical.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_sickbay_vulcan_star: Right on time. To the second, I imagine.
I arrived at the appointed time. Precisely.
I am functioning within acceptable parameters.
I do not have complaints. I have observations.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_buff: Buffer's running a point-oh-three percent drift. Point-oh-three.
The pattern buffer hums half a tone flat. You can't hear it. I can.
It's inside tolerance. Well inside. That's not the point.
By the book, no. By me, yes.
Somebody comes up through this buffer with their nose a millimetre left.
You'd notice. Every mirror, for the rest of your life, you'd notice.
I'd think it was my face.
I wouldn't notice. My nose is already left.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_cal_: Once for the book. Once for the captain. Once for me.
Because the first two were for other people.
Does the third one ever find anything?
And does the third one differ?
Once. In April. A phase variance in the secondary coil.
Never. That's why I trust it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_fix_: Aligned. Listen. That's the right note.
You'd hear it if you were on the pad.
When did you last take a day off?
I sleep. In that chair. With the beacon alarm on my wrist.
Tuesdays. Kess makes me. I spend it thinking about the buffer.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_kess: Kess wants the whole system certified before tonight's window.
Lieutenant th'Zoran's schedule has a beam at nineteen hundred.
Kess is right. Kess is always right. It's exhausting.
Andorians. They say what they think. Usually that you're late.
Maybe. A beacon's live. If they get to it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_leav: I'll take my coffee somewhere safer.
Mind the rail on your way out.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_rhel: Why not get engineering up here?
Rhel's got a warp core to apologise to. I can handle a buffer.
Rhel came up once. Spent an hour telling the coils they were brave.
The drift went down. I don't want to talk about it.
They've been very steady since. Don't tell him.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_scot: Didn't someone survive in a buffer once? For decades?
Wasn't there an engineer who lived in a pattern buffer?
Montgomery Scott. Seventy-five years, on a loop. Old history now.
Captain Scott. Jury-rigged a buffer and came out seventy years later.
With this buffer? Four seconds and I'm sweating.
Don't give Rhel ideas. He'd try it with the core.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_spar: Funny, isn't it. Whoever broke the ship left this alone.
Why leave us the transporters? If you wanted us stuck?
I think about that every shift.
I've asked myself a thousand times.
Maybe they needed it. Maybe they didn't think it mattered.
Maybe they wanted us able to watch. And unable to leave.
It's working, that's what counts. And I'm keeping it working.
They made a mistake. This room is their mistake. I like that.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_star: Please don't put your coffee on the console.
Hands off the pad rail, if you would. Just calibrated it.
Sorry. It's a railing. People lean on railings.
It's a mug. It's got a lid.
It's a transporter. People lean on it, people end up in Kansas.
That console holds eleven thousand terabytes of somebody's atoms.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_stay: Mind if I stay and watch?
Can I watch the next check?
Stand there. Not there. There. Don't touch anything.
If you're quiet. And the coffee goes outside.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_buffer_fuss_why_: This thing is all we've got. You know that?
No warp. No impulse. No comms. This. This room. That's it.
Everyone who comes home, comes home through here.
Every one of the eleven that's come back, came back on that pad.
I hadn't thought of it that way.
So, yes. I'm going to fuss. I'll fuss all day.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_e_arg: The captain argued. Came down here herself. Stood on the pad.
Vale stood right there and argued with them on an open channel.
She could have. She asked instead. She said it was their call.
She said the work mattered. She said please be careful.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_e_jun: And then late June. Two days.
Did you try to bring them up?
Couldn't you get them all up?
I tried. For two days I didn't leave this room.
Every lock I could hold, I held. Some beacons, I couldn't find.
The ones who weren't near a badge. Or who'd lost it running.
Some were too far. Some were underground. Some went quiet.
I know. I'll know it better one day.
Since July, somebody's been finding them. One at a time.
And now somebody down there brings them. One by one.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_e_wor: They were in the middle of it. Market days. Radio. The harvest.
Six months of study, half done. They wanted to finish it.
In February, the planet was having a very ordinary week.
The ship was stuck, not sinking. And the county was fine.
We could beam them any time. They could reach us. So they stayed.
There was no reason to come up. The transporters worked.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_eleve: And the surface team? The eleven?
Eleven stayed for the fieldwork. Some are back. Some aren't.
Eleven chose to stay. I've brought up some of them. Not all.
I keep the others at the bottom of the list. Blank line after each.
The ones still down there have a line each. Waiting to be filled in.
Lindqvist. She was in my study group.
I think the line's blank. That's all I know.
Blank means not yet. I'm not writing anything else in it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_hope_: I hope you fill them in.
I hope you get to write them all.
Me too. I've got a very nice stylus saved for it.
Come by any time. I'll be here.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_list_: Novak. Came up bleeding and apologising for the carpet.
Tamura. Came up singing. Wouldn't say what.
Haddad. Off a roof. Refused the medic. Fainted two steps later.
Sato. Asked if we still had coffee. First thing. Not hello.
Every one. You don't forget the first thing a person says.
I'm not going to forget them. That's not how it works.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_memor: How do you remember them all?
It's not memory. It's the pattern. You hold a person, once.
Every pattern goes through the buffer. I watch every one.
For four seconds, a whole person is numbers on my console.
For a moment you're responsible for every atom of someone.
I'd never thought of it like that.
It's the best job on the ship.
Heavy. And the best job there is.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_other: What about the people who aren't ours? From the county?
Could you bring up someone from down there? A civilian?
If someone put a signal on that pad, I'd take them.
The captain's ruled. Anyone who reaches us. No questions.
They'd go on the list like anyone else. First words and all.
They'd get a line. Same as everyone. Same ink.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_start: What's that padd you're always holding?
Names. Everyone who's come up on this pad since February.
Everybody I've brought home. And the ones I haven't. Yet.
You don't have to show me.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_every_name_staye: Can I ask why they stayed?
Why did they stay down, the eleven?

Fieldwork. That's the answer everyone gives. It's true.
For the work. Every one of them. The survey wasn't finished.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_admit_1_1: All right. I hate it. I've always hated it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_admit_1_2: I don't like being taken apart. There. I said it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_admit_2_2: A lot of people don't. More than you think.

Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_admit_5_2: He did. He was fine. Mostly.

Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_after_2_2: Told you. Your nose is exactly where you left it.

Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_after_3_2: I want to do it again. No. Never.

Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_deny_2_1: I'm fine. I love transporters. They're my favourite thing.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_deny_2_2: I'm perfectly calm. This is my calm face.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_explain_1_1: Here's how it works. You stand. I lock. Four seconds. Done.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_explain_1_2: You won't feel a thing. A tingle. Like cold water on the arms.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_explain_2_2: Where am I, for those four seconds?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_explain_3_1: In my buffer. With me watching every atom. I don't blink.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_explain_3_2: Right here. On this screen. I've never lost anyone off this pad.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_explain_5_1: Not once. Not in nine years.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_go_1_2: Up you get. Hands at your sides.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_go_2_2: Don't count down. Just do it.

Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_history_2_2: Harder. Weaker lock. Moving target. And it still works. Every time.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_history_3_1: If they can do it from a rooftop...
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_history_3_2: Then I can do it to the cargo bay.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_joke_1_1: Think of it this way. The version of you that walks off is brand new.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_joke_1_2: Philosophers have argued about that since Cochrane. Don't think about it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_joke_2_2: That is the worst thing you could have said.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_joke_3_1: Sorry. Bad joke. Old transporter chief's joke.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_joke_3_2: Yes. Sorry. That one's for engineers.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_start_1_1: I don't have to go today, do I?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_start_1_2: I'm on the roster for a test beam.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_start_1_3: Is it true the survey team's using the pad today?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_start_2_1: Pad two, ten hundred, you and a crate of sample jars.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_fear_start_2_2: Your name's on Kess's list. Ship to cargo bay. Short hop.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_afte: Clear the board. Log the time. And wait for the next one.
Log it. Go and tell the captain. Then come back.
Do you want me to tell her?
No. I'll do it. It should be me.
Come with me. It's easier with two.
Beacon lost. Not found. Not lost. Beacon lost.
The time, and the place. And nothing else. Not yet.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_flic: Could be the badge. Could be the rain. Could be nothing.
Could mean they're walking. Could mean the badge is in the mud.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_gone: I don't know. That's the thing about it. You never know.
Could be the badge failed. Could be anything. It just stops.
That doesn't mean anything. Does it?
It doesn't. It means I can't hear them. That's all.
It means the line's blank. And I leave it blank.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_kess: Kess will want the log. She hates this part.
I have to log it for Kess.
Andorians feel everything. They just say it in fewer words.
She signs these and goes to the gym for an hour. Every time.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_lock: No. No, that's a reflection. A mast. Sorry. Sorry.
It's the shuttle's carrier. Not the badge. Not them.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_star: Beacon's still on the board. Ensign Kowalczyk. North of the river.
Still live. Ensign Ferreira. Somebody accepted the call this morning.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_talk: A little. Botany. Talked to plants the way Rhel talks to the core.
We played cards on Thursdays. Terrible at cards. Worse at lying.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_lost_beacon_wait: Stay. Don't talk. Or talk. Either.
Does it ever just come through, at the last minute?
Have you had one come in right at the end?
Once. Eleven hours, fifty minutes. Came up laughing.
Twice. Once with four minutes left. I nearly cried.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_c: That's another one. That's another one.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_d: Where... is this the ship? Am I on the ship?
I was on a roof. I was on a roof a second ago.
Oh. Oh, it's so quiet. Is it over?
You're aboard the Adirondack. You're safe. Sit down for me.
Easy. You're home. Sit before you fall down.
My hands won't stop. Sorry. Sorry.
That's normal. That's your body catching up. Breathe.
Nothing to be sorry for. Breathe with me. In. Out.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_g: They were everywhere. The streets. I couldn't get to the badge.
I was in a school for a week. I heard them on the stairs every night.
I lost my tricorder in a river. I had to wait. Just wait.
Not now. You don't have to tell us now.
I ate cat food. I want someone to know. I ate cat food.
I kept my combadge in my sock. Every night. In my sock.
Noted for the medical log. You'll never eat it again.
The best thing you ever did. It got you here.
I can't stop talking. Is that normal?
It's normal. Keep going if it helps.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_l: Logging. Rescue, time, name. One more home.
Adding it to the list. Another one home.
Wasn't me. Somebody down there did the hard part.
I just pressed the button. The hard part was on the ground.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_o: The others. Is anyone else back? Castellan? Reyes?
Did the others make it up? We got separated in June.
Some. Not all. I'll get you the list when you've rested.
A few are aboard. Sickbay has the names. You'll see them.
One thing at a time. You first.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_s: Let me look at you. Tricorder. Don't move.
Scanning. Hold still for me, {ensign}.
Dehydrated. Two cracked ribs. Scratches. No bites, no fever.
Malnourished. A sprained ankle. You've been on it for days.
I'm fine. I'm fine.
Is that bad?
I ran on that ankle.
You're not fine. You'll be fine. There's a difference.
You're alive. Everything else, we can fix.
Sickbay. Now. Doctor Anwar's waiting.
Can you walk? Lean on me. It's not far.
Can I have a shower? A real one?
I'd kill for a bath.
Is there food? Real food? Not out of a tin?
Water shower. Doctor's orders.
Grieg will have something hot.
Sonic first. Then Grieg's soup. It's very good soup.
Lock! I have a lock. Energising.
Signal's up. Locking on. Energising.
Combadge signal. Holding it. Holding. Energising now.
Got them. Got them. They're aboard.
Materialised. We have them.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_t: Please tell me this is real.
I heard the chime. I didn't think it would work.
Medical team to the transporter room.
Stay on the pad a moment.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_rescue_arrives_w: Someone found me. There was someone. On the ground.
Who was that? Someone came. They had a tricorder.
We don't know who. Somebody's been answering the distress calls.
We never know. Just a signal, and a lock, and then you.
They didn't say a word. Just held up the tricorder and nodded.
I think I said thank you. I don't remember. I hope I did.
Whoever it was, they got you here.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_shepard_arrival_: We'd asked her to come up every week since February. She wouldn't.
The captain ordered it once. Shepard politely declined. For months.
You can decline an order?
How did she get away with that?
Not really. But she was the only one who understood the ground.
She said she was the only one who knew how this century boils water.
She called and said: Energise. Now. Just that.
She didn't chat. No hello. Just, bring me up. Please. Now.
Was she hurt?
Was she in trouble?
No. Not a scratch. But her voice. I'd never heard it like that.
Not physically. She was pale as the pad when she arrived.
She said a chair had been moved. In her shuttle. That was all.
She kept saying, the chair was moved. The chair was moved.
A chair?
That's it? A chair?
Nothing taken. Nothing broken. A chair in a different place.
That's all. And she'd been in that county through all of June.
That's what got her to come up?
After everything?
After everything.
A chair. I've thought about that a lot.
Is she all right now?
How is she, these days?
She argues with everybody. That means she's fine.
She's on the channel every day. She fusses about her shuttle.
And she fills out cargo requests for lamps. So, yes.
She's Shepard again. That's the best sign there is.
Good.
I'm glad.
Lamps. Of course.
Were you on duty when Shepard came up?
You beamed Shepard up, right?
They say you brought Lieutenant Shepard up. The ninth.
The ninth of July. Oh-seven-fifty. I'll never forget it.
I did. The ninth. Morning. She called it in herself.
She didn't bring a thing. Not a bag. She left it all on the shuttle.
Empty-handed. The lamps, the tapes, the chair. She left all of it.
Her collection? The tapes?
She left the tapes behind?
I asked. She said, somebody down there should have them.
She said, they're where they need to be. Then she gave me a look.
Somebody like who?
What kind of look?
Like she knew who. Like she wasn't telling.
Like there was someone down there she was counting on.
The captain came through that door at a run. I've never seen her run.
Vale got here in ninety seconds. From the ready room. Four decks.
What did she say?
What happened?
Nothing. Put her arms round her. Held on. Neither of them said a word.
She said, you stubborn, stubborn woman. And then she hugged her.
The captain hugged someone?
Vale? Our Vale?
Don't tell anyone I told you.
I didn't see it. I was very busy.
What did she say, when she got here?
What were her first words?
She stood there. Then she said, I'm sorry. I stayed too long.
She said, Is the captain up? And then, I need to sit down.
And then?
What did you say?
I said, welcome home, Lieutenant. What else is there?
I said the captain was on her way. She was already running.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_again_1: Go on. Beam it back. Carefully.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_again_2: Coordinates: transporter room pad one. Twice. Out loud.
Pad one. Pad one. Pad one. Energising.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_again_3: Crate on the pad. Well done.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_again_5: Leave it. Grieg will want it back.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_again_6: Can I log that as a successful transport?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_again_7: It counts. I'm writing a note in the margin.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_done_1_: That'll do for today. Go and apologise. Take flowers.
Enough. Go and say sorry in person. Bring something.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_done_2_: Flowers? Where do I get flowers?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_done_3_: Hydroponics. Tell them it's an emergency.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_fine_1_: Crate arrived in cargo bay three. Right side up.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_fine_2_: Well done. Again, with two crates.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_galley_: That's the galley. You beamed rations into the galley.
That's Grieg's galley. You sent a crate to the galley.
At least it's the right department?
Onto the counter? Or into the soup?
Grieg's on the comm. She says thank you. And never again.
Grieg says it's in her bread dough. And she's coming up here.
She said she'd bring a rolling pin.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_lesson_: Lesson one. Read the coordinates twice. Out loud.
This is why we check the bay first. Every time. Twice.
I'll check three times from now on.
Good. Everybody does it once. I sent a chair to the brig.
Don't worry. My first one went into a warp nacelle. It was fine.
They kept it. It's still there.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_quarter: That's crew quarters. That's someone's bunk.
You put thirty kilos of ration packs in someone's quarters.
Section nine. That's the counselor. That's Tren's quarters.
Section nine. Lieutenant Tren. She's off shift. She's asleep.
She's on the comm. She wants to know if it's a metaphor.
Tren's calling. She'd like to talk about why I did it.
Tell her it's a training exercise.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_start_1: Right. Today we beam a crate of ration packs to the cargo bay.
Training exercise. One crate. Pad to cargo bay three. Simple.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_start_3: Never say that in this room.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_steps_1: Lock the crate. Confirm the destination. Then energise.
Target the crate, target the bay, check the phase, then energise.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_steps_3: Right. Confirm arrival with the bay.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_wrong_1: Bay three says... they don't have it.
Hm. Cargo bay says no crate.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_wrong_2: What do you mean, they don't have it?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_wrong_3: I did. It says it arrived. It's just not in the bay.
The system says materialised. The bay says it's empty.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_training_wrong_5: Deck four, section nine, cargo... oh. Oh no.
Deck four, section... that's not a cargo bay, is it.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_ask_1_: What do the ensigns say about them? The ones who came up?
Did anyone describe them? Height, anything?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_ask_2_: Novak said they smelled of woodsmoke and had a very old tricorder.
Haddad said they wore something odd. Not a uniform. Maybe a uniform.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_ask_3_: Sato swore they hummed the whole time. Badly.
Tamura says they talked to her. Kept her awake. Told her jokes.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_ask_4_: That's not much to go on.
So a person. Probably human. Maybe.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_gratef: Whoever they are, I'd shake their hand.
I owe them. We all do.
I'd give them my holodeck time. A whole week of it.
I'd give them my replicator ration. All of it.
Grieg says she's saving a pie for them. A real one.
I'd just like to say thank you. To a face.
They might come up one day.
Maybe they're standing in this room. Who knows.
You'd notice a stranger on this ship.
I'll keep an eye out. Anyone who looks lost and competent.
That's half the ship. Lost and competent.
Then I'll thank all of you, just in case.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_kess_1: Kess ran the numbers. Somebody's on the ground and on the shuttle.
Kess says it's the shuttle's signal every time. The same crew.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_kess_2: The shuttle? Shepard's shuttle? It's parked down there.
Somebody's using Shepard's shuttle? With the lamps?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_kess_3: Somebody's living in it. Somebody's using the sensors.
Somebody found it and learned it. And now they answer our calls.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_kess_5: If she does, she's not saying.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_start_: I heard the chime at two a.m.
Is it true there was another rescue?
Ensign Moreau. Came up at oh-two-hundred. Sickbay has her.
Another ensign. Twenty minutes after the beacon lit.
That's quick work. Whoever it is.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_theory: A survivor. A local who found a combadge. That's my guess.
One of the eleven, maybe. Someone we don't know is alive.
A local wouldn't know how to use a tricorder.
One of ours would've come up by now. Surely.
Unless they don't want to. Shepard didn't, for months.
Maybe they're too busy. It's a big county.
Or maybe it's somebody we'll never meet.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_twice_: What if there's more than one of them?
The pattern's different sometimes. The signal comes from new places.
Could be. Some nights two beacons. Some nights none.
A team of strangers saving our people.
Which is either very good or very strange.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_who_1_: So who's doing it? Who's down there?
Nobody knows who's answering the calls? Honestly?
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_who_2_: Honestly? No. A combadge in their hand, and that's all I see.
We get a lock on the ensign. Never on the one who found them.
Print_Text_TREK_CREW_tr_who_beams_who_3_: The ensigns never get a name. A face, sometimes. A nod.
They say someone arrives, scans them and steps back.
